uncovered.finding: There is no AI packet anywhere in the plan. All three Gemini routes (app/api/chat/route.js, app/api/learn-mode/grade-explanation/route.js, app/api/written-practice/evaluate/route.js) are untouched by P0-P13, and the phrase 'AI', 'tutor', 'grading', 'Gemini' and 'prompt' do not appear in the plan at all. Every AI finding below is therefore uncovered by construction, not by oversight in one packet.
uncovered.whyItMatters: The AI features are the only thing the EUR0.99 premium tier sells (grading, tutor, written evaluation). A 2-4 week remediation that never opens those three files ships all the retention work while the paid surface stays broken, which is the wrong end of a 16-active / 40-cancelled churn problem.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14 AI correctness (single solo packet, all three routes + the two client components; one session is enough)

uncovered.finding: Grading system prompt says 'You are a friendly Edexcel A-Level Economics & Business examiner' (verified at grade-explanation/route.js:49) - wrong qualification - and passes no section keyIdea, misconception, examMatters or mark scheme. The model grades against invented criteria.
uncovered.whyItMatters: A premium student's explanation is praised or penalised against UK GCE expectations and content the notes never taught, and the grader cannot flag the misconception the section explicitly warns about. This is the single clearest 'I paid and it is wrong' moment in the product.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14 AI correctness

uncovered.finding: No retry and no schema on grading: the route regex-parses JSON out of free text, and a parse failure surfaces as a generic error with feedback left null so the Grade button silently stays.
uncovered.whyItMatters: The premium student clicks Grade, waits, gets an error, and has to click again with no idea whether their typed answer survived. Intermittent failure on a paid action reads as the product being broken.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14 AI correctness (Output.object + zod + one automatic retry)

uncovered.finding: maxTokens is not a valid option in AI SDK v6 (package.json pins ai ^6.0.116); it is passed in all three routes - chat/route.js:121 (800), grade-explanation/route.js:58 (300), written-practice/evaluate/route.js:149 (800) - so no output cap is applied anywhere. The audit fix text says 'all three routes' but the plan should be told the third is written-practice/evaluate, which the plan never mentions.
uncovered.whyItMatters: Uncapped generation can run past the 15s maxDuration on the grading route (student sees a timeout on a paid click) and makes tutor/evaluate cost per call unbounded - on a EUR0.99/month product that is a margin question, not a nit.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14 AI correctness (rename to maxOutputTokens in all THREE routes)

uncovered.finding: Tutor system prompt hardcodes the Economics unit range as WEC11-WEC12 (verified at chat/route.js:95) instead of WEC11-WEC14, injects no section content, and gives 20-mark essay structure advice that contradicts the practice guidance. The daily-limit response is a raw JSON body rendered to the student.
uncovered.whyItMatters: A Year 13 asking about WEC13/WEC14 is talking to a tutor that has been told those units are out of scope, and gets structure advice that contradicts the practice card they just read. Contradiction between two premium surfaces is worse than either being silent.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14 AI correctness

uncovered.finding: ExplainItBack is a dead end: free users get no response of any kind after typing, the tutor fallback button is unreachable for everyone, onExplainAttempt is never wired, and the typed draft is not persisted.
uncovered.whyItMatters: This sits on the last step of every block, including step 0 of introductory-concepts where 167 of 192 users are stuck. The student is asked to write, writes, and the app does nothing; at completion their Explain It Back score reads 0 regardless of effort.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14 AI correctness, or fold the free-user path into P2 since it is a Learn Mode container concern

uncovered.finding: Subscription lookup uses .single(), so any user with more than one user_subscriptions row (cancelled + active, the exact shape of a 40-cancelled/16-active base) resolves to free and gets a 403 after the client has already shown the button.
uncovered.whyItMatters: A student who cancelled and resubscribed - the cohort the founder most wants back - pays and then cannot use the paid feature. No packet verifies whether duplicate user_id rows actually exist in production, which is a ten-minute query that should precede the fix.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14 AI correctness, with a duplicate-row count run first

uncovered.finding: In-memory rate limiter does not enforce anything on Vercel's serverless runtime, and chat/route.js duplicates it with a second Map rather than importing lib/rate-limit.js.
uncovered.whyItMatters: The advertised 50/day grading and 30/day tutor limits are advisory only, so Gemini spend is unbounded per user. Low student harm, but it is the one finding in this slice that can cost real money while the founder is conserving tokens elsewhere.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14 AI correctness (shared Supabase daily-counter table)

uncovered.finding: QuestionCard's keyboard handler treats any key whose name starts with a-d (Ctrl, Alt, ArrowDown, Backspace, CapsLock) as an answer selection.
uncovered.whyItMatters: Ctrl+Tab or an arrow-key scroll silently selects an answer and lights 'Check answer'; the next Enter records a wrong answer into SM-2. On a mobile-heavy base this mostly bites desktop/keyboard users, but it corrupts the scheduling data for everyone it touches, and every other Smart Practice fix is measured against that corrupted data.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14b Smart Practice engine (solo code packet) - one-line fix, requires e.key.length === 1 and ignores ctrl/meta/alt

uncovered.finding: Confidence is never collected in Smart Practice at all, while Learn Mode's InlineQuiz prompt asks for confidence AFTER the answer is revealed, auto-dismisses after 4s, writes to localStorage and is read by nothing. computeNextReview already accepts confidence.
uncovered.whyItMatters: Lucky guesses schedule identically to secure knowledge, so a student who guesses B accumulates 'mastered' cards (repetitions>=3) they cannot answer - and P3 is about to make that scheduling server-side and authoritative. P3 hardens a scheduler whose only quality signal is missing. Sequence this before or with P3.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14b Smart Practice engine - must land before or inside P3

uncovered.finding: InlineQuiz wrong answers feed only a local completion counter: they do not enter the review schedule, the mistakes tab, or the post-test. The remediation branch is dead code.
uncovered.whyItMatters: The retention loop P3 is building is fed by nothing from Learn Mode itself. A student can get every inline quiz wrong and the system's model of them is unchanged - so 'review schedule server-side' persists an empty signal correctly.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: P3 (extend its scope) or NEW: P14b

uncovered.finding: 'This question will come back' is shown on every wrong answer but wrong items are never re-appended to the in-session queue, and the summary's 'RETRIED' stat counts questions that were never retried.
uncovered.whyItMatters: The app makes a specific promise six times in one session, breaks it within that session, and then reports on the summary screen that it kept it. That is a trust failure a student can verify unaided.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14b Smart Practice engine

uncovered.finding: After a productive session the same topic shows 'No questions available' with no explanation, because everything is scheduled and nothing is due.
uncovered.whyItMatters: The audit calls this the most direct code-level cause of the 'doesn't cover all topics' complaint. The plan addresses the content-depth cause (P8-P10) and nothing addresses the message that makes a fully-covered topic look empty. It is a copy-plus-state change, cheap, and it protects the perceived value of all the content work.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14b Smart Practice engine - distinguish 'up to date, next due in Xh' from 'no content', add 'Practise anyway'

uncovered.finding: Pre-test questions reappear as the same block's inline quiz in ~50% of sections, and the post-test is the identical 3 questions in identical order. Plus PreTest.jsx:135 prints 'Perfect - your brain is now primed' after a 0/3 score.
uncovered.whyItMatters: The pre/post delta on the completion screen - the app's only claim of learning - measures whether the student remembers 'it was B' ten minutes later. If the plan later cites pre/post improvement as evidence the remediation worked, it will be citing an artefact. P2 makes the pre-test optional and remembered but does not touch the overlap, the post-test identity, or the sarcastic 0/3 copy.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: P2 (extend) or NEW: P14b - exclude the union of blocks' quizIndices from the pre-test pool; sample different post-test items

uncovered.finding: Learn Mode only ever surfaces ~5 of each section's 25 questions; the other 20 are reachable only via the paywalled Quiz tab, Quick Fire, or /practice, which lives outside the section tabs.
uncovered.whyItMatters: Every question P5, P6 and P7 fix is 80% invisible to the students the plan is trying to retain. Mapping unmapped questions to blocks and pre-selecting the section in the completion-screen CTA is the cheapest possible multiplier on the content packets, and no packet does it.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14b, or add to P5 as a mapping deliverable

uncovered.finding: Session composition draws randomly across selected topics, so a 20-question session can skip several of the topics the student deliberately chose, and there is no session-length picker.
uncovered.whyItMatters: A student who selects their six weakest topics may practise three of them. Round-robin interleaving is also better pedagogy than blocking, which matters given the pedagogy critique elsewhere in the audit.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14b Smart Practice engine

uncovered.finding: Topic picker: every unit collapsed by default showing '0 / N', the unit-number badge is an undiscoverable select-all, chips carry no question or due counts, and the copy frames practice as what the student is 'assessed on'.
uncovered.whyItMatters: This is the entry screen to Smart Practice and it looks empty on arrival - the same first-screen abandonment shape as the 87%/82% Learn Mode step-0 losses the plan is built around. Question counts need no auth, so anonymous students can be given a reason to start. The plan fixes Learn Mode's first screen and leaves Smart Practice's untouched.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14b Smart Practice engine (pair with P2 as the other first-screen fix)

uncovered.finding: Smart Practice serves all 25 questions per section free while the section Quiz tab paywalls the same bank after 2, and the QuizTab preview scores 2 questions with no retry while the CTA copy implies it is the student's score.
uncovered.whyItMatters: The gating story is incoherent in both directions: a student who finds /practice concludes the paywall is arbitrary, and one who does not believes they get 2 questions per section. With 40 cancelled against 16 active at EUR0.99, what premium actually buys is a founder decision the plan never schedules - and it constrains P14's upsell copy in ExplainItBack and InlinePractice.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P-decision (founder, not a code session): one written gating policy, before P14/P14b

weaklyCovered.finding: 64% of correct answers are option B and options are never shuffled at render (769 MCQs)
weaklyCovered.whatIsMissing: P5 is scoped as a workflow with 43-way content fan-out. Rebalancing correctIndex across A-D is content work and fits. Shuffling at render is not: it is a shared seeded-permutation helper plus a selected-index remap in six separate renderers (QuestionCard, PreTest, InlineQuiz, QuickFireDrill, QuizTab, PracticeEngine), and a content workflow will not produce it. Split P5 into P5a (code: one shuffle helper, six call sites, verified by a test that the same question gives different option orders across seeds and still marks correctly) and P5b (content rebalance). Also: shuffling at render breaks any stored answer keyed by option index - check SM-2 records and pre/post-test comparison before shipping it. And note the interaction with the pre/post-test finding: shuffling makes 'it was B' recall harder but does not make the post-test a different test.

weaklyCovered.finding: Examiner review of 10 questions: evaluative command words (Evaluate/Assess/To what extent) forced into MCQ stems, hedged-vs-absolute option tells, contestable keys against the IAL definition, mixed currency conventions
weaklyCovered.packet: P5 Quiz bank hygiene + P4 Validator v2 quality gate
weaklyCovered.whatIsMissing: The quality gate lists position balance, no duplicate stems, and subsection tagging. It does not encode: no essay command words in MCQ stems, at most one absolute-word ('always', 'never', 'all') distractor per item, one currency convention per subject, and key defensibility against the Edexcel IAL definition. Without those rules in validator v2, P5's 43-way fan-out has no rule to check against and these defects survive the packet that was supposed to catch them. Note the first two are mechanically checkable (word lists); key defensibility is not and belongs on the IAL teacher sign-off list, which currently covers only rewritten sections and reshaped practice questions, not MCQs.

weaklyCovered.finding: InlinePractice never lets the student write in any mode; all three modes render the same read-only guidance text
weaklyCovered.packet: P6 / P7 Practice questions, Economics and Business
weaklyCovered.whatIsMissing: P6 and P7 reshape 215 practice questions to real IAL tariffs and levels-based guidance. Nothing in the plan makes the component that renders them accept an answer. The outcome is 215 correctly-reshaped questions delivered through a card where the student reads, clicks reveal, reads a mark skeleton and moves on - the practice card still practises nothing. Add an answer box plus a self-mark checklist derived from the '(n marks)' fragments to P6/P7's definition of done, or the content work is unobservable. Reuse exists and the plan misses it: components/written-practice/WrittenQuestionCard.jsx already posts to app/api/written-practice/evaluate/route.js, which is already IAL AO-based; that route also carries the maxTokens bug (line 149) and is never mentioned in the plan.

weaklyCovered.finding: Units 3-4 carry 2 blocks / 4 sub-sections / 10 questions against Units 1-2's 5-8 blocks / 10-24 sub-sections / 25 questions
weaklyCovered.packet: P8-P10 (nine rewrite sections, Unit 3 Business first)
weaklyCovered.whatIsMissing: P8-P10 deepen nine named sections. The finding is about every Unit 3-4 section's question bank and block count, which is wider than nine, and about the absence of an honest depth signal in the meantime. Smart Practice over a whole Unit 3 selection tops out around 60 questions, which is also why the 'No questions available' state fires so fast for Year 13s. Add to P8-P10 (or a cheap solo packet): per-section 'N questions' on the topic chips and section header, so a Year 13 revising WEC13/WEC14 for the January series can see what exists rather than concluding the app does not cover their year.

coverage.sliceVerdict: This slice is essentially unplanned. Of 23 findings, 4 are genuinely covered (all of them incidentally, by P2's practice-index line and P5's dedupe/off-topic lines), 4 are weakly covered, and 18 have no packet - including every AI finding, because the plan contains no AI packet at all and never names the three Gemini routes. That is a structural gap, not a set of misses: the paid tier is grading + tutor + written evaluation, the churn number is 16 active against 40 cancelled, and the plan's 2-4 weeks never opens those files. Two additions close most of it cheaply: P14 AI correctness (one solo session across the three routes - IAL-correct grading prompt with section context, zod schema plus retry, maxOutputTokens, WEC11-14 in the tutor prompt, .single() fix, shared rate-limit store) and P14b Smart Practice engine (one solo session - keyboard guard, confidence capture, requeue wrong items, honest empty state, topic-picker counts and select-all). Two sequencing points matter: P14b's confidence capture must land before or inside P3, or P3 makes an unfed scheduler authoritative; and P5's render-time shuffle is code, not content, so it cannot ride the 43-way fan-out and must be checked against any stored index-keyed answers. One item is not a code packet at all - the Smart-Practice-free-versus-Quiz-tab-paywalled contradiction is a founder pricing decision that gates the upsell copy in two of the P14 fixes and should be settled first.

uncovered.finding: Section API returns 152 KB raw / ~39 KB gzip with no Cache-Control, refetched on every section switch, and ~40% of it is tabs Learn Mode never renders. No client-side cache of loaded sections.
uncovered.whyItMatters: On the target markets' networks (school Wi-Fi, ~1-2 Mbps effective, 200-400 ms RTT) every section open and every re-open is a 1-2 s blank screen, and the blank screen shows the 'being prepared' copy (see below). This is a direct contributor to the 825/1093 step-0 abandons and it is a one-session fix (a header plus a Map).
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14 Network and render performance (Cache-Control + fields param + client section cache)

uncovered.finding: Glossary highlighting rebuilds ~372 RegExp objects and re-splits HTML per paragraph on every LearnModeTab re-render (quiz tap, menu toggle, transition flag). No useMemo, no React.memo on NoteSection.
uncovered.whyItMatters: On the mid/low-end Android phones typical of HK/MY/PK/LK, every quiz option tap, confidence tap and Next tap stalls visibly and scrolling janks afterwards. Combined with the 350 ms artificial Next delay this pushes each interaction toward 0.5 s+, which reads as a broken app rather than a slow one.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14 Network and render performance

uncovered.finding: No visual hierarchy between Key Idea, body, Real Example, Misconception, Exam Matters — identical size, weight and card treatment, only hue differs; the amber misconception is visually louder than the Key Idea; step.blockTitle (the chapter) is never rendered as an eyebrow.
uncovered.whyItMatters: This is the reason P2's 'one subsection per step' will not be enough: halving the step still leaves five equally-weighted coloured cards per subsection with no reading order. A student scanning on a 390px phone cannot tell which card the exam rewards, so the page reads as an undifferentiated wall and they bounce. It is also the cheapest half of the deferred 'step anatomy redesign'.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P13a Step visual hierarchy (Key Idea dominant, secondary cards demoted, blockTitle eyebrow, Takeaway strongest) — run before or with P2

uncovered.finding: Glossary tooltip is mouseover-only: no click/touch toggle, no tap-outside dismiss, no tabindex/aria-describedby, no keyboard path. Same term is re-underlined in every card and paragraph of a step.
uncovered.whyItMatters: On a mobile-heavy cohort the app's glossary feature is effectively non-existent: the dotted underlines are noise, a tap fires a synthetic mouseover so a 280px fixed tooltip appears and sticks until the next tap or scroll. Definitions are a core value prop for EAL students in HK/SG/MY/PK/LK; today they cannot be opened deliberately or closed deliberately.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P13a, or extend P13 with an explicit 'glossary term interaction' bullet

uncovered.finding: Zero ARIA across step widgets and no :focus-visible styling anywhere; recall items are click-only <div>s; Skip/move buttons are bare glyphs (× and ▲) with no labels; heading order is broken.
uncovered.whyItMatters: Keyboard and switch users cannot complete a reorder recall at all, and screen-reader users hear 'multiplication sign, button'. P13's five named items do not include accessibility beyond contrast, and the recall-widget redesign is deferred to week 3+, so today this is owned by nobody. It is also a procurement blocker if the founder ever sells to schools.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P13b Accessibility pass (focus-visible tokens, button semantics, aria-labels, heading order)

uncovered.finding: Tab bar puts onClick/role=tab/aria-selected on a <div> while the real <button> inside carries tabIndex={-1}; no arrow-key handling on the tablist.
uncovered.whyItMatters: The app's primary navigation cannot be reached or activated by keyboard at all, and screen readers announce tabs that are not focusable. Trivial fix (move the handler and drop tabIndex={-1}) that no packet claims.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P13b Accessibility pass

uncovered.finding: Content HTML is injected unescaped (no &, <, > escaping before the bold/italic regexes), and the glossary definition is interpolated into a String.replace template so $1 / $& / $` in a definition are interpreted as replacement patterns.
uncovered.whyItMatters: Latent today but the plan is about to run P6/P7/P8-P10/P11 — mass content regeneration by agents. A generated definition containing 'below $1 a day' (plausible in development-economics content) will silently render the term name instead, and any generated text containing '<' will lose words on screen. Fix the escaping BEFORE the content-generation packets, not after.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: P0 or P4 (validator/pipeline hardening) — must land before P6

uncovered.finding: Horizontal space: .rl-note-section keeps 24px padding on mobile and the stepper rail consumes 52px with no <768px override, leaving a ~230-257px text column (~175px inside FlowChain cards) on a 360-390px phone.
uncovered.whyItMatters: Text wraps every 5-6 words, FlowChain titles wrap to two lines, and the whole step is 30-40% longer than it needs to be — for one number circle. This compounds the 5,300-5,900px step height that P2 is trying to halve; without it, P2's 'one subsection per step' lands at ~2,700px and still feels endless. P13's bullet list ('contrast, tap targets, diagram sizing, text size, reduced motion') does not include layout width.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: P13 — add an explicit 'mobile layout width: kill the rail, cut padding' bullet; sequence with P2

uncovered.finding: Only 4 of 9 tabs fit at 360-390px; the remaining 5 sit behind a 28px fade with no chevron, no 'More' sheet, and no scroll-into-view on active change.
uncovered.whyItMatters: Flashcards, Quiz, Tutor and Extras — the features being charged for — are undiscoverable on the primary device. With 16 premium vs 40 cancelled at EUR0.99/mo, a paying student may never have seen what they paid for. This is a churn finding sitting in the CSS slice and no packet touches it.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: P13, or NEW: P15 Monetisation surface (with the pricing/paywall work)

uncovered.finding: Loading state on section switch renders the same copy as the empty state: 'Content for this section is being prepared.' No skeleton, no spinner, previous section is unmounted immediately.
uncovered.whyItMatters: Every slow section open actively tells the student the topic does not exist yet. Paired with the uncached 152 KB payload, the 1-2 s network gap is presented as 'we haven't written this'. This is arguably the single cheapest abandon-reduction fix in the whole audit and no packet names it.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14 Network and render performance (pair with the caching fix)

uncovered.finding: 'Next' is disabled for a hard 350 ms timer before the step swaps, and the lmStepEnter/exit animations that would justify the delay are never applied.
uncovered.whyItMatters: The core progression action feels broken: button greys, nothing happens, content jumps. P2 owns 'sticky Next' (where the button is) but not 'Next is artificially laggy' (whether pressing it works). On a slow phone, with the glossary re-highlight on top, this is the felt cost of advancing — directly relevant to the 75% who never advance.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: P2 (add as a bullet) or NEW: P14

uncovered.finding: AnimatedTabBar instantiates 5 springs + 2 motion elements per tab (~45 springs) on mobile, where the animated indicator is disabled anyway; framer-motion is not lazy-loaded.
uncovered.whyItMatters: Pure waste on every shell render on the lowest-powered devices in the user base, and it contributes to the 167 KB gzip shared bundle that must download before Learn Mode hydrates.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P14 Network and render performance

uncovered.finding: Quiz confidence row auto-dismisses after 4 s and remediation slides in 1 s after a wrong answer, shifting layout twice while the student is reading the explanation.
uncovered.whyItMatters: The Next button and the following card move out from under a planned thumb tap, producing mis-taps at exactly the moment the student is deciding whether to continue. No packet covers InlineQuiz layout behaviour (P5 covers the quiz bank's content, not its rendering).
uncovered.suggestedPacket: P13, or NEW: P13a

uncovered.finding: The previous step's recall widget is rendered ABOVE the new step's content, pushing reading ~310px down so steps 2+ open on a quiz before any teaching and before the section title.
uncovered.whyItMatters: P2's 'duplicate recall' bullet addresses a different finding (the same recall shown twice back-to-back, LearnModeTab.jsx:346). Placement is separate and unowned. Combined with the pre-test gate, the first three things a new student meets are tests, not teaching — the plan's own headline problem. Deferring this to the week 3+ 'step anatomy redesign' leaves it live through every content packet.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: P2 — add 'recall renders after the step's first NoteSection, collapsed, with a from-last-step cue'

uncovered.finding: FlowChain subtitle splits on a literal ' — ' separator that content almost never uses, and flow step titles are not run through parseInlineMarkdown, so they alone cannot carry bold or glossary terms.
uncovered.whyItMatters: Silent no-op today, but P6-P11 will have agents authoring flow chains at scale; if they emit '–' or ' - ' the subtitle silently vanishes, and no validator rule catches it. Either document the convention in the content skill or accept {title, subtitle}.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: P4 (validator v2) plus a one-line component change

weaklyCovered.finding: One Learn Mode step is ~5,300-5,900px on a 390px phone (7.5-8.5 screens, 13-15 cards)
weaklyCovered.whatIsMissing: P2 takes only option (a) from the finding. Halving 5,600px leaves ~2,800px = 4+ screens, still with no progressive disclosure. The finding's options (b) collapse RealExample/Misconception/ExamMatters into an accordion and (c) sticky bottom bar are what actually bound the height, and (b) is the same intervention as the uncovered visual-hierarchy finding. P2 also states no acceptance criterion — set an explicit target (e.g. no step exceeds ~2.5 viewport heights at 390px) or the packet cannot be verified.

weaklyCovered.finding: Diagram SVGs render at 270px with ~5px effective label text; 'enlarge' modal is only ~25% bigger with no pinch-zoom
weaklyCovered.whatIsMissing: 'Sizing' understates the fix: it needs a minimum font-size enforced inside processSvg (scale text to >=14 viewBox units) and a full-screen modal with touch-action:pinch-zoom, not just max-width:100%. Worse, the sequencing is backwards — P12 authors eight new diagram types across 20 Business sections BEFORE P13 fixes the renderer, so every newly authored diagram ships unreadable on the primary device and gets judged as 'passive' again. Move the renderer fix ahead of P12.

weaklyCovered.finding: Light-theme contrast failures (recall text #d4bfff at ~1.4:1, card labels, reorder/fill-in prompt invisible)
weaklyCovered.whatIsMissing: The fix is token definition plus replacement of ~13 hardcoded hex values across globals.css and the recall components; the packet brief should name the tokens (--rl-amber-text, --rl-teal-text, --rl-blue-text, --rl-green-text, --lm-purple-text/bg, --recall-accent) and ban --text-dim for text. The plan also proposes no contrast check in validator v2 and no CI guard, so the next content or CSS packet can reintroduce it. Note the finding also says the label size must rise to 11px minimum — a sizing change hidden inside a 'contrast' bullet.

weaklyCovered.finding: iOS Safari auto-zoom on focusing the 13px Explain-It-Back textarea
weaklyCovered.whatIsMissing: A generic 13px→15px body sweep does NOT fix this: iOS zooms below 16px, so the rule must be exactly font-size:16px on .lm-explain-textarea and .lm-recall-textarea at all widths. Name it separately in the brief or it will be missed and the page will stay zoomed after typing, hiding the Next button.

weaklyCovered.finding: Recall arrow buttons ~12x20px, dismiss/more/hint targets far below 44px, chips and blanks under 40px
weaklyCovered.whatIsMissing: These targets live in ReorderRecall/FillInRecall, whose redesign the plan explicitly defers to week 3+ ('recalls deliberately wait for the step redesign'). The plan must say whether P13 is allowed to touch deferred widgets; otherwise either the CSS lands on components about to be rewritten (wasted) or the fix silently falls out of both packets. A student who completes five topics in a week opens the sidebar to a column of red slivers sitting next to green completion ticks. Nothing in the plan ends a block with a Checkpoint (score, memory-strength change, 'next block: X, 4 min' / 'stop here, review due Thursday'), and nothing adds a minutes badge per block. CompletionScreen still fires only at section end. This falls inside the 'step anatomy redesign' deferred to week 3+.
uncovered.whyItMatters: Median activity span is ~1 hour total and 75% never pass step 0, so essentially no student ever reaches the only reward screen in the product. A student who does three good screens on a phone gets no bankable moment and no reason to open the app again tomorrow.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: Fold into P2 (LearnModeTab is already open in that packet) rather than week 3+ — a block-end checkpoint is a single new component plus a block boundary that P2 is already redrawing.

uncovered.finding: Pattern 3 — hint before answer, then re-queue the miss in the same session. Not in any packet. InlineQuiz still reveals the correct answer after 200 ms, and the missed item is never re-served before the block can end.
uncovered.whyItMatters: A student gets it wrong, is shown the answer, learns nothing from the miss, and leaves the block with the misconception intact — then the same misconception reappears in the PostTest and the section feels pointless.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: P2 (same file set) or NEW: P-MissLoop — show the section keyIdea as a hint plus one retry before reveal, and push misses into an end-of-block 'clear your misses' round. Explicitly no hearts/energy penalty.

uncovered.finding: Pattern 5 — two-layer progress with levels that can go down. P3 fixes the boolean-column bug and stores furthest step, which is completion only. There is no session-score-vs-memory-strength split, no Familiar/Proficient/Mastered, no demotion on a failed due review, and no Mastered-only-via-later-mixed-test rule. The research is explicit that completion alone is never the mastery signal and that it is demotion that makes a level credible.
uncovered.whyItMatters: A student sees a bar that only goes up and knows it does not mean they can answer the questions; a parent has nothing to look at; and there is no number the premium routing layer can be sold against.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: P3 — at minimum land the SCHEMA now (level enum + memory-strength/last-seen per section per user), even if the UI ships in week 3. Shipping P3 as furthest-step-only guarantees a second migration and a second pass over the same endpoints.

uncovered.finding: No instrumentation packet. The plan's headline metric (825/1093 starts never leave step 0) came from a one-off query, and nothing in the plan re-runs it or captures per-step/per-block events going forward. There is also no event-level activity log, which pattern 10 later needs to compute each user's habit window.
uncovered.location: Plan has no packet; research-fact-check-1.md:98 (reminders computed from activity timestamps)
uncovered.whyItMatters: Fourteen packets ship over 2-4 weeks and nobody can say whether the step-0 cliff moved, so the next decision is made on the same blind guessing as this one — and when reminders are built in week 3 there is no history to time them from.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: Fold into P3 — add a learn_mode_events table (user, section, step, block, event type, client timestamp + tz offset) and a saved funnel query rerun at the end of every packet.

uncovered.finding: Pattern 7 — confidence self-rating (1-5) on TakeawayCard and on the PostTest explanation reveal, feeding the 1/3/7/14 schedule. Absent from every packet and from the week-3+ list.
uncovered.whyItMatters: Given 197/272 recall exercises are unusable and 24 sections have none at all, there is currently NO per-item retention signal for most sections — so any spacing the app does is uninformed. A 1-5 tap is the only signal available that needs no content authoring at all.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: P2 or the new P-MissLoop — one widget, writes to the same per-section row P3 is already creating. Cheapest item in the entire research report.

uncovered.finding: Pattern 11 — test-date-driven pacing. The plan never mentions exam series anywhere. IAL sits January and June; the research flags that a UK single-May/June assumption is wrong, and the report itself lists onboarding only as a week-3+ line with no exam-date content.
uncovered.location: Plan line 48 ('onboarding and reminders', deferred); research-fact-check-1.md:100
uncovered.whyItMatters: It is September 2026, so the active cohort is sitting January 2027 units; without asking the series the app cannot say 'N sections to Proficient, M study days left, ~X min/day', which is the one framing that makes a Jan-series student open it daily in October.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: NEW: P-Pacing (or fold the single question into P2's optional-pretest screen) — one onboarding question (series + which units), one derived pacing line on the subject page.

uncovered.finding: Pattern 10 — streak by ANY activity plus reminders in the user's own timezone window. Deferred wholesale to week 3+ with no design constraints recorded, so the deferred work carries no memory of the two facts that matter: streak must be extended by any activity (Duolingo's decoupling raised 7+ day streaks by >40%) and notifications must fire at the user's observed local hour, max 2/day, never a fixed UTC time.
uncovered.whyItMatters: Students are in HK/SG/MY/PK/LK/KR/ME. A reminder cron built on a UTC default pings a Karachi student at 05:00, they disable notifications once, and the retention channel is dead permanently.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: Keep the build in week 3+, but record the constraints in the P0 backlog file AND land the timestamp capture in P3 now, or week 3 has no habit window to compute.

uncovered.finding: Pattern 2 (second half) — a question within seconds of each content chunk. P2 delivers 'one subsection per step', which halves the reading, but nothing in the plan puts a question on every step; InlineQuiz/InlinePractice still only attach to the last step of a block, so a block is still several question-free screens. The research notes the questions need no new authoring — a 'which of these is the misconception?' MCQ can be generated from the existing per-section misconception field.
uncovered.whyItMatters: A student on a phone still reads three screens before being asked anything, which is the exact pattern Save My Exams is criticised for and the reason input-only revision does not produce exam output.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: P2, or a small generation workflow alongside P5 that emits one misconception-MCQ per subsection from content that already exists.

uncovered.finding: Pattern 6 (second half) — a 'My misses' pool built from InlineQuiz/PostTest wrongs. P3 persists the review schedule but nothing anywhere collects or replays wrong answers. This is the single feature Seneca charges premium for.
uncovered.whyItMatters: Wrong answers evaporate at the end of a session, so a student repeats the same mistakes across weeks and the app has nothing personalised to show them when they return — and nothing worth EUR0.99 either.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: P3 (store) + the new P-Freemium (surface, and make it the metered layer).

uncovered.finding: Pattern 8 (second half) — free self-mark against a 3-bullet indicative list, with AI marking as the visible upgrade moment. P6/P7 reshape the 215 practice questions to real IAL tariffs and produce markschemes, but no packet gives free users any way to close the loop with them; Explain-It-Back stays premium-only free-text grading.
uncovered.whyItMatters: The reshaped markschemes P6/P7 spend two whole packets producing are invisible to the 40 free users, so the free loop still ends in reading rather than output, and the moment where a student would feel the value of paying never happens.
uncovered.suggestedPacket: P6/P7 must emit the 3-bullet indicative content list as a required field, plus a small UI packet (or P2) for the self-mark panel and the 'see how an examiner would mark this' upsell.

weaklyCovered.finding: Pattern 1 — replace the pre-test gate with an opt-in 'test out' that REWARDS passing
weaklyCovered.whatIsMissing: P2 only removes the gate; it adds no reward. The research's point is that opt-in placement works because passing buys you something — Up Learn's pre-video checks tick off the video, Khan's 100% first try jumps two levels. Without 'Already know this? Test out (3 Qs)' framing and a pass that marks the matching blocks Familiar and jumps past them, a rational student always taps skip and the pre-test becomes dead code rather than a placement signal. Note the dependency: there is no Familiar state to write until the P3 mastery schema exists, so P2 and P3 must agree on it or P2 ships a skip button and nothing else. Also unaddressed: the 3 MCQs are drawn at random from the section bank (PreTest.jsx:9-10), so a 'pass' currently means nothing about which blocks to skip.

weaklyCovered.finding: Pattern 4 — drop the immediate bottom recall, KEEP the spaced recall from the previous step
weaklyCovered.whatIsMissing: P2's one-line scope is ambiguous about which of the two recall widgets goes. The research names this precisely: delete the immediate recall of the section currently on screen (LearnModeTab.jsx:397-403) and keep the spaced recall of the previous step (LearnModeTab.jsx:345-360) — the latter is listed as a genuine differentiator no reading-first competitor has. Written as 'duplicate recall' a session could remove the wrong one. Second gap: removing the immediate recall while all 338 recall replacements are deferred to week 3+ strictly reduces the number of questions per screen in weeks 1-2, which cuts against pattern 2; P2 needs a replacement question landing in the same packet.

weaklyCovered.finding: Pattern 6 — surface due reviews on the landing/overview instead of interrupting
weaklyCovered.whatIsMissing: P3 covers persistence (moving it off localStorage, which is right and also fixes cross-device loss). It does not cover the two behavioural halves: (a) killing the auto-launch on mount (StudyApp.jsx:319-337) which interrupts rather than invites, and (b) a '3 reviews due (approx 4 min)' card at the top of the subject page. Persisted-but-still-buried reviews change nothing a student can see.

weaklyCovered.finding: Strength to keep — inline diagrams as a differentiator, with DiagramLabelDrill as the DEFAULT interaction
weaklyCovered.whatIsMissing: P12 authors the missing 20 Business diagrams and P2 fixes a matching bug, but neither states the research's actual recommendation: make the label drill the default interaction rather than the passive image. Authoring 8 new Business diagram types as passive images reproduces the reading-heavy problem in a new medium and wastes the one Economics-side advantage over Seneca.

weaklyCovered.finding: Strength to keep — per-section misconception / examMatters / realExample richness
weaklyCovered.whatIsMissing: The quality gate lists structural rules (reorder sources, unique fill-ins, quiz key balance, tariffs, diagram refs) but never requires that rewrites PRESERVE misconception/examMatters/realExample. The research identifies these as the fields that make Revvy richer than Seneca's card text and comparable to what students pay SME for — and pattern 2's per-step question generation depends on misconception existing. A rewrite agent optimising for readability can quietly drop them across nine sections. Add a validator v2 rule in P4: every subsection must carry all three fields, non-empty and non-duplicated.

weaklyCovered.finding: The week-3+ deferral of retention mechanics as a whole
weaklyCovered.whatIsMissing: The deferral is the wrong call for a churn problem, and the split is drawn along the wrong axis. Nine of fourteen packets (P5-P12) improve content accuracy — that is, they improve material for students who are already staying, while 75% never get past step 0 and premium users cancel inside a month. Nothing shipping in weeks 1-2 gives a returning student a reason to return. The cheap retention set — block checkpoint, hint-then-requeue, confidence rating, due-reviews on the landing screen, test-out reward, freemium boundary — is roughly two packets of work, mostly inside LearnModeTab and the progress schema that P2 and P3 are already opening. Suggested reshuffle: pull those into weeks 1-2 alongside P1-P4, and push P11 (accuracy sweep) and P12 (diagrams) to week 3+; both improve content nobody currently reaches. Secondary sequencing risk: as written, LearnModeTab is restructured in P2 and then restructured again by the deferred 8-stage step redesign, and the progress endpoints are migrated in P3 then migrated again for the mastery model — two rewrites of the same files, which is the opposite of token conservation.

wellCovered: Reorder-only-from-real-flow-chains, unique fill-in answers, distractor banks and no letter hints — pattern 4's authoring RULES are explicitly in the quality gate (plan lines 53-55), so deferring the 338 recall rewrites to week 3+ is a defensible call rather than a gap.
Pattern 8's content half — P6/P7 reshape all 215 practice questions to real IAL tariffs and command words with levels-based guidance, and P7 anchors every Business item to an extract.
Pattern 2's reading-volume half — P2's 'one subsection per step' directly attacks the 613-word / ~5,900px step.
Pattern 6's plumbing — P3 moves the review schedule off localStorage to the server, which also fixes cross-device loss for a mobile-heavy cohort.
Pattern 1's gate removal — P2 makes the pre-test optional and remembers the choice, which unblocks the step-0 cliff even though the reward half is missing.
coverage.sliceVerdict: Not adequately planned for. Of the 12 patterns, the plan addresses roughly three-and-a-half, and every one of those is the mechanical half of a pattern whose behavioural half is missing (gate removed but no test-out reward; reading halved but no per-step question; schedule persisted but never surfaced; markschemes reshaped but free users cannot use them). Six patterns — freemium boundary, block checkpoints, hint-then-requeue, two-layer mastery, confidence rating, test-date pacing — appear nowhere, and the two that are consciously deferred (streak/reminders) carry no recorded design constraints and depend on activity-timestamp capture the plan does not schedule. The deferral of retention work to week 3+ is the plan's main error: it front-loads nine content packets that improve material 75% of users never reach, while the cheap changes that act on the step-0 cliff and on EUR0.99 churn sit behind them, and it commits to rewriting LearnModeTab and the progress schema twice. Two structural fixes matter most: land the mastery/level and event schema inside P3 rather than a furthest-step-only migration, and add a freemium-boundary packet, because nothing else in fourteen packets touches conversion.

uncovered.finding: Nothing in the plan carries the actual tariff sets, and the two subjects' sets are different and mutually destructive if confused. Economics (Appendix 6, spec p.68) permits ONLY: Define 2, Calculate 2 or 4, Draw 4, Explain 4, Analyse 6, Examine 8, Discuss 14, Evaluate / To what extent 20. Business (Appendix 6, spec p.56) permits ONLY: Define 2, Calculate 4, Construct 4, Explain 4, Analyse 6, Discuss 8, Assess 10 (Units 1/2) or Assess 12 (Units 3/4), Evaluate 20. Economics has no Assess, no 10, no 12, no Construct, no Outline. Business has no Examine, no Draw, no 14, no Explain 6, no Outline. The plan says only 'real IAL tariffs'.

The current bank is uniformly {Define 4, Explain 6, Assess/Analyse 10, Evaluate 20, Outline 4} — literally every one of the 215 items is wrong, so there is no correct in-repo example for an agent to pattern-match against.

coverage.sliceVerdict: The plan is strong on the doc's editorial and content-rule recommendations and weak on everything that lives in runtime state: strength, confidence, scheduling, and what completion means. Deferring the FULL step anatomy to week 3+ is defensible — P2's one-section-per-step removes the wall, which is half of the doc's stated cause of the 75% stall, and the doc's own card 3-7 work depends on content that does not exist yet. It is NOT defensible to defer cards 1, 2 and 8 for the two entry sections losing 87% and 82%: those are a line of copy, one reused MCQ with confidence captured before answering, and a next-review date, and they are the only thing in the plan that puts an interaction inside the first screen. The plan's most serious structural error is P3: it lands a 'furthest step' schema in week 1 for a product whose mastery model is explicitly per-item evidence over time, which forces a second migration and discards two weeks of attempt data. Add the attempts/review tables and the confidence-before-answer capture to P3, and add the completion gate to P2 — otherwise the plan's own success metric (completion rate) still measures key presses, and no before/after comparison it produces will be trustworthy.
