coverage.sliceVerdict: Not adequately planned. Sampling: read all 79 accuracy, all 79 quiz and all 56 practice items in full (214/214), all 401 structure items in full across all 43 sections, all 215 topFix items (rank 0-4 for every section) at 260 chars, and a random sample of 18 of 340 specGap items; plus programmatic classification of the structure and accuracy sets to get per-category and per-section counts. Of the 401 structure items I judge roughly 250-265 covered or explicitly deferred (about 80 in the nine P8-P10 rewrite sections, ~30 by P2's code fixes, ~22 by P12's Business diagrams, ~70 under the deferred recall pile, ~40 under the deferred spec gaps, ~15 by P5/P6/P7/P11) and roughly 135-150 with no owner. The largest single orphan is block metadata re-authoring — 83 structure items across 40 sections, and the rank-0 topFix in about 20 of them; P2 fixes the code that reads quizIndices/practiceIndices/diagramRef but nothing rewrites the data, and 13 sections have no wiring keys at all. It should become its own packet (P5b, 43-way mechanical fan-out on a cheap model) placed after P2 and before P5, because P5 renumbers the bank it points into. Two structural coupling errors matter more than any individual gap: P5's only exits for an off-topic MCQ are move-or-delete, but ~40 of the quiz findings are 'on-spec for this section, never taught here', whose fix sits in the 340 deferred spec gaps — so P5 as written will delete on-spec assessment while leaving the pre-test contamination that drives the 75% step-0 abandonment (measured at 71-75% probability of an untaught pre-test item in two sections); and no packet produces the IAL command-word/tariff/spec ground-truth artefact that P4, P5, P6, P7 and P8-P10 all consume, on the exact fact the codebase already got wrong 215 times out of 215. Also correct P1 to cover all 18 sev=critical items (6 accuracy + 8 quiz + 4 practice, not 6+8), and re-scope P11: only 33 of its 79 accuracy items are examples — 17 are false claims about what IAL examiners reward, 15 are body/keyIdea contradictions and 10 are diagram geometry.

critiques.lens: Delivery management — sequencing, packet sizing, session-to-session continuity, and reversibility for a solo founder working ~2-4 weeks with an AI

problems.problem: Every paying student's spaced-repetition state is keyed to array position, and P1/P5/P6/P7/P8-P10 all renumber those arrays. This is not a versioning nicety — it is silent, undetectable corruption of the product's core value for the 16 people paying for it.
problems.evidence: /Users/arongijsel/Claude APP/economics-next/scripts/create-practice-progress-table.sql: `question_index INTEGER NOT NULL` with `UNIQUE(user_id, section_id, question_index)`. That one table is the junk drawer for five entity types by prefix (quiz raw id, `fc-`, `lm-`, `wp-`) — see app/api/practice/progress/route.js, app/api/flashcards-practice/progress/route.js, app/api/learn-mode/progress/route.js. Meanwhile the content items carry no ids at all: in audit/content-sections/economics__price-determination.json the 25 quiz objects have keys {question, options, explanation} and the 5 practice objects {marks, command, guidance} — no id field anywhere. P5 dedupes, reorders and moves items between sections; P6/P7 reshape all 215 practice items; P8-P10 rewrite whole sections. Each of those shifts indices under live rows with no error and no log.
problems.fix: Split P4 and move its first half to position 1. P4a (before ANY content push): mint stable ids into every quiz/practice/flashcard/recall/diagram item; add `item_id TEXT` to practice_question_progress; backfill it from the current index using the audit snapshot as the authority; switch all five API routes to read/write by item_id; keep question_index only as a dead column. Only then is any content packet safe. Explicitly decide and record what happens to rows whose item is deleted (P5 dupes) — orphan or drop.

problems.problem: There is no rollback story at all, and the plan does not notice that it already owns 90% of one. Pushes are single whole-blob overwrites across eight separate tables with no transaction, so a half-finished packet leaves a section with new content and stale quiz/practice/diagrams.
problems.evidence: Push pattern is `.update({ data: section.notes }).eq('section_id', section.id)` (scripts/update-business-unit1-rich-notes.mjs:1407-1408) repeated per table across 64 `from('section_content')`, 31 `section_notes`, 13 `section_quiz`, 11 `section_practice`, 23 `section_diagrams`, 10 `section_flashcards`, 5 `section_extras` call sites. But audit/content-sections/*.json is already a committed, git-tracked, 6.4MB full snapshot of live content for all 43 sections across exactly those tables — nobody has written the script that pushes it back.
problems.fix: Add to P0 (about an hour): `scripts/snapshot-section.mjs <ids...>` writing timestamped per-section JSON into audit/snapshots/, and `scripts/restore-section.mjs <file>` that replays it to all eight tables. Make it a hard rule that every content packet starts by snapshotting only the sections it will touch and ends with a commit. Treat the existing audit/content-sections snapshot as the t=0 baseline and say so in the plan, because it stops being current the moment P1 pushes.

problems.problem: P3 is described as 'fix the boolean column' but it is really a data-model decision that overlaps P4 and can corrupt the dashboard the moment it starts working. Learn Mode writes have been failing silently for the whole life of the feature.
problems.evidence: app/api/learn-mode/progress/route.js writes `last_result: 'correct'` and `` `post:${postTestScore}` `` into a column declared `last_result BOOLEAN` (create-practice-progress-table.sql), with no error check on the awaited upsert — so there is no historical Learn Mode data to migrate, only new writes. It also writes `question_index: -1` as a completion marker and `repetitions: isComplete ? 3 : 1`. The dashboard (app/api/progress/dashboard/route.js:64-73) counts EVERY row in the table toward mastered/learning, stripping only the `fc-` prefix and treating repetitions>=3 as mastered. The moment P3 makes Learn Mode writes succeed and merges `lm-` back like `fc-`, step markers get counted as mastered questions and the -1 sentinel joins the review queue.
problems.fix: Merge P3 into P4a as one 'progress data model' packet: real columns or a proper enum for result, a `kind` column instead of prefix-in-the-id, item_id instead of question_index, and the -1 sentinel replaced with an explicit completion field. Doing it twice costs more than doing it once, and doing P3 alone ships a visibly wrong dashboard.

problems.problem: P5 is not fan-out-safe as written. Its 'move off-topic items to the section that teaches them' step makes 43 parallel agents write into each other's sections — a merge conflict inside a database, with last-write-wins and no detection.
problems.evidence: Packet text: 'off-topic items moved to the section that teaches them', declared as 'Workflow, 43-way fan-out'. Each section's quiz lives in one row's JSON array (section_quiz), overwritten wholesale; two agents both appending to economics__price-determination clobber each other.
problems.fix: Split: P5a = within-section only (wrong keys, duplicate stems, key balance) — safe 43-way fan-out. P5b = cross-section moves, done solo as one planned migration with a written source→destination manifest. Also pull 'shuffle at render' out of P5 entirely: it is a code change in the quiz component, it interacts with index-keyed progress, and it belongs in P4a.

problems.problem: P7 (Business practice) is mis-sized because the thing it depends on does not exist. 'Every item anchored to an extract' means authoring 20 case-study extracts from scratch, not reshaping existing questions.
problems.evidence: audit/README.md states every IAL Business question is anchored to a named extract line. No extract field exists in the live content: audit/content-sections/*.json practice objects carry only {marks, command, guidance}. content/data-response/ holds only 6 files, all Unit 1.
problems.fix: Make extract sourcing an explicit decision before P7 starts (author new, reuse content/data-response/, or licence/adapt from past papers — with the copyright question answered), and budget P7 as two sessions minimum: one to author extracts, one to anchor questions. Or cut scope to Units 1-2 for the January series and defer 3-4.

problems.problem: P8-P10 at three full section rewrites per packet is the single most likely place the plan stalls. These are the packets the audit itself says need a specialist, and they also sit behind the unnamed teacher sign-off.
problems.evidence: Plan: 'The nine rewrite sections — three packets of three ... one agent per section plus verification.' Section blobs are large (43 sections = 6.4MB of snapshot); a rewrite touches content, notes, quiz, practice, flashcards, extras for that section. Quality gate: 'One IAL teacher signs off rewritten sections and reshaped practice questions before they go live' — no name, no cost, no turnaround.
problems.fix: One section per packet, nine packets, and accept that this is most of week 3-4 rather than pretending it is three sessions. Name the teacher and book their review slots in week 1, or move sign-off off the critical path by publishing behind a draft flag and reviewing after.

problems.problem: P2 is eight unrelated defects in the largest component in the app, sold as one packet, and two of them collide with P3's rewrite of the same progress write path.
problems.evidence: P2 lists: one subsection per step; pre-test optional and remembered; practice index bug; diagram matching; duplicate recall; 5 unfinishable fill-ins; sticky Next; duplicate subsection title. 'Pre-test optional and remembered' and 'practice index bug' both write through app/api/learn-mode/progress/route.js, which P3 rewrites.
problems.fix: Split P2 into P2a (step/subsection restructure + sticky Next + duplicate title — layout, no persistence) and P2b (pre-test memory, practice index, diagram matching, fill-ins — all persistence-adjacent), and run P2b immediately after the merged P3/P4a so it writes against the fixed model.

problems.problem: 'One packet per session then clear context' has no carrier artefact specified, so session N will re-derive what sessions 1..N-1 did — the exact token cost the whole operating model exists to avoid. The tracker is one clause inside P0 with no schema.
problems.evidence: Plan P0: 'audit backlog per-item in repo, progress tracker, DB dump moved out of temp.' No definition of what the tracker records. Operating model rule 2 says 'No session loads the whole audit' but nothing says what a session loads instead.
problems.fix: Specify the handoff pack as three files read at the top of every session, total under 300 lines: audit/PROGRESS.md (one row per packet: status, commit sha, sections touched, snapshot path, validator result), audit/DECISIONS.md (irreversible choices later packets must respect — ids minted so never renumber, recall widgets frozen until the step redesign, tariff lists canonical), and audit/NEXT.md (the brief for the next packet, written at the END of the previous session while context is still loaded). Writing NEXT.md before clearing context is the cheapest thing in the plan and the plan does not have it.

problems.problem: No git discipline, on a tree that is already dirty and five months stale. Without commit-per-packet there is no way to answer 'what did the last session actually change', and the restore script has nothing to diff against.
problems.evidence: `git status --porcelain` shows 8 modified files uncommitted right now (app/command-words/page.js, app/contact/page.js, app/glossary/page.js, app/guides/page.js, app/ial-revision/january-2027/page.js, app/ial-revision/june-2026/page.js, app/model-answers/page.js, app/past-papers/page.js) plus untracked audit/README.md; latest commit is cd6aed4 and the brief says nothing has landed since 20 April 2026.
problems.fix: P0 step 1: land or revert the 8 dirty files so the tree is clean, then branch `remediation/2026-09`. Rule: a packet is not done until it is committed with the packet id in the subject. The commit sha goes in the PROGRESS.md row; that pair is the resumable state.

problems.problem: Nothing defines what an interrupted packet looks like, and a 43-way fan-out is the most likely thing to die halfway. There is no record of which sections a packet has already pushed.
problems.evidence: Quality gate defines only 'validator run over all 43 sections' at packet end; there is no per-section completion record anywhere in the schema (no push log among the 22 tables in use).
problems.fix: Add a `content_push_log` table (section_id, packet, script, git_sha, pushed_at) and have every push script write a row. Resuming an interrupted packet becomes `sections_in_packet - sections_in_log`, computable in one query instead of reconstructed from memory. Define packet-done as: validator green on all 43, push log complete, commit made, PROGRESS.md updated — all four.

problems.problem: Everything ships straight to live content read by 211 students during term, with no draft state and no flag. Rollback-by-restore is minutes of wrong content in front of real users in every timezone in the cohort.
problems.evidence: All push scripts write the live row directly (`.update({data}).eq('section_id', ...)`); no is_published/draft/version column appears in any script or the content tables.
problems.fix: In P4a, add a draft JSONB column (or a versions table keyed by section_id + version) so pushes land unpublished and go live as one UPDATE per packet. Same work as versioning, and it turns rollback into a single statement rather than a replay of eight tables.

problems.problem: The plan defers the fix most likely to move its own headline metric, and never re-measures. Thirteen packets land before anything addresses the 613-word, 5,900px step that is the probable cause of the 87%/82% first-screen loss.
problems.evidence: Plan, Week 3+: 'explicitly deferred, not dropped: full step anatomy redesign (the 8-stage step...)'. Headline is 75% of opens never passing step 0. No packet contains a measurement checkpoint against funnel_aggregates.json.
problems.fix: Insert a cheap P2.5 right after P2a: split step 0 only, on the two entry sections that lose 87% and 82%, and nothing else. Re-read the funnel two weeks later and let the result decide whether the full 8-stage redesign is worth week 5. Add 'read the funnel again' as an explicit dated step, not a packet — it costs nothing and it is what keeps a solo founder believing the other twelve packets are worth doing.

problems.problem: P12's size is unknown, which in practice means it is large. The plan says 'diagrams' but the schema stores checklists, so it is unclear whether this is authoring content, building a renderer, or both.
problems.evidence: audit/content-sections/economics__price-determination.json diagrams entries are {title, checklist:[...]} — descriptions of what a correct hand-drawn diagram contains, not drawings. P12 lists eight distinct Business diagram types across 20 sections and is marked 'Solo plus review'.
problems.fix: Before scheduling P12, decide the output format (checklist text like Economics, or actual rendered SVG). If SVG, that is a component-building packet plus a content packet per diagram type, i.e. 4+ sessions — put it after the January series, not inside the 2-4 weeks.

problems.problem: The validator lands after the packets whose rules it encodes are already specified, so the rules get written twice.
problems.evidence: P4 'Validator v2 — semantic checks' comes after P1/P2/P3; the tariff rules it must enforce are already fully written down in audit/README.md and audit/raw/research-ial-spec-coverage.md (IAL Economics: Define 2, Calculate 2/4, Draw 4, Explain 4, Analyse 6, Examine 8, Discuss 14, Evaluate 20, no 10-mark, no Assess/Outline; IAL Business: ... Assess 10 or 12, Evaluate 20 ending in a recommendation).
problems.fix: Encode the tariff, key-balance, fill-in-uniqueness and diagram-reference rules in P4a from the audit files that already state them, so P5/P6/P7 are pure application of a checked rule rather than re-derivation of it.

resequencing: P0 becomes 'clean tree + snapshot/restore + handoff pack', not just preservation: land/revert the 8 dirty files, branch, write snapshot-section.mjs and restore-section.mjs, create audit/PROGRESS.md, audit/DECISIONS.md, audit/NEXT.md. The audit corpus itself is already preserved and committed (audit/, 59 tracked files, 6.4MB) — do not re-do that part.

Move P4 to position 2 and split it: P4a (stable item ids minted into content + practice_question_progress migrated from question_index to item_id + all five API routes switched + draft/version column + diff-based push + validator rules encoded from audit/raw) runs BEFORE P1. P4b (semantic content checks, live violation list) can follow later. Yes to the question asked: P4 must precede P1 — but for the progress-key reason, not the versioning reason.
Merge P3 into P4a. Both change practice_question_progress; doing them separately means migrating the same table twice and shipping a knowingly wrong dashboard in between.
P1 (6 false examples + 8 broken quiz items) runs third, as the first push through the new diff-based, snapshot-backed path — small blast radius makes it the ideal smoke test of P4a.

Split P2 into P2a (layout: one subsection per step, sticky Next, duplicate title) and P2b (persistence-adjacent: pre-test memory, practice index bug, diagram matching, duplicate recall, 5 fill-ins). P2a can run any time after P0; P2b must run after P4a.

Insert P2.5 immediately after P2a: split step 0 on the two entry sections only (87% and 82% loss), then a dated funnel re-read two weeks later. This is the only packet before week 3 that targets the headline metric.

Split P5 into P5a (within-section quiz hygiene — safe 43-way fan-out) and P5b (cross-section item moves — solo, single manifest, never fan-out). Move 'shuffle at render' out of P5 into P4a as a code change.
P7 gains a precursor decision on where Business extracts come from, and is budgeted as two sessions; consider cutting it to Units 1-2 for the January series.

P8-P10 becomes nine one-section packets, not three three-section packets. Fold P11's internationalisation of UK examples INTO each rewrite packet rather than running it as a separate sweep over sections that were just rewritten; keep P11 as fact-checking the 73 high-severity examples in the sections that are NOT being rewritten.
P12 (Business diagrams) moves after the January series unless the output format decision shows it is checklist-only.
Book the IAL teacher's review slots in week 1, before P6/P7/P8-P10 start. An unnamed external reviewer on the critical path of eleven packets is a schedule bomb.
whatIsGood: 'Preserve first, never re-audit' is the right instinct and is already executed: audit/ is committed, tracked and indexed, with a README that tells a fresh session exactly which file answers which question. That README is the best artefact in this project.

audit/content-sections/*.json is a full snapshot of live content for all 43 sections across every content table. The plan does not realise it, but this is a working t=0 rollback baseline — it needs only a restore script.
Putting the command-word tariffs directly in audit/README.md, above the fold, is exactly right: it is the fact every content packet needs and the one most likely to be re-derived expensively.
'The validator replaces review' is the correct economic argument for a solo founder — checking 43 sections by script instead of 43 agents. The only error is landing it after the first pushes.
'Workflows only for real fan-out, code packets run solo' is a good, cheap heuristic and it is correctly applied to most packets.
Deferring recall exercises until after the step redesign, with the reason stated ('so they are not regenerated into the same broken widgets'), is the single best sequencing decision in the plan.

The quality gate's 'every content packet ends with the validator run over all 43 sections, not just the ones touched' is right, and is the mechanism that would catch a cross-section fan-out clobber if P5b is done as recommended.

critiques.lens: Growth lead owning the churn number (activation + paid retention), reading the plan against the live code in /Users/arongijsel/Claude APP/economics-next

problems.problem: The plan spends 11 of 14 packets improving a FREE surface in order to move a PAID churn number. Learn Mode is free; the paywall sits on flashcards, quiz, mistakes, tutor, extras. A cancelling subscriber is not cancelling because of Learn Mode content quality — they never paid for it. No packet in P0–P13 touches tutor, flashcards, mistakes or extras at all.
problems.evidence: /Users/arongijsel/Claude APP/economics-next/components/StudyApp.jsx:25-27 — FREE_TABS = {learn-mode, content, notes, diagrams, practice}; PREVIEW_TABS = {flashcards, quiz, extras}; PREMIUM_TABS = {mistakes, tutor}. P5 (quiz bank) is the only packet that lands on a paid surface and it is sixth in the order.
problems.fix: Label every packet with the number it moves: activation/step-0 (free funnel) vs paid retention. Require at least one paid-surface packet in week 1 — P5 qualifies and should move up. If the theory is 'better free Learn Mode → more upgrades', state that conversion hypothesis explicitly and instrument it, because the plan currently asserts a churn fix while working exclusively on the free tier.

problems.problem: Step 0 is not a long content step for most students — it is a pre-test. 'One subsection per step' (P2) does not touch the screen where the 75% actually die. This answers question (2): it is not sufficient on its own.
problems.evidence: /Users/arongijsel/Claude APP/economics-next/components/LearnModeTab.jsx:249 — `if (showPretest && currentStep === 0) { return <PreTest .../> }`; :34-37 — showPretest defaults true whenever `quizData?.length > 0` and the user is not resuming. So a first-time student's first screen is 3 MCQs on material they have not been taught, drawn from the bank where the key is at option B 64% of the time and is never shuffled (PreTest.jsx:9 uses a biased `sort(() => Math.random() - 0.5)`).
problems.fix: The step-0 fix is: make the pre-test opt-in or replace it with a single predict-question ('Test yourself first' / 'Just teach me'), AND shorten the first card set, AND keep one subsection per step. All three, in one packet, before anything else content-side. One of the three alone will not move it.

problems.problem: The 75% figure is derived from a write path the plan itself says is broken, and there is no instrumentation to prove any packet worked. The plan commits 2-4 weeks against a number it cannot currently reproduce or re-measure.
problems.evidence: /Users/arongijsel/Claude APP/economics-next/app/api/learn-mode/progress/route.js:25-62 writes `last_result: 'correct'` and `last_confidence: \`pre:${preTestScore}\`` and never checks the upsert's error — failures are silent, so completions are undercounted. Pre-test completion writes nothing server-side (PreTest.jsx:45-60 → localStorage only, plus recordPretest into lib/strength.js which is localStorage-only, :3 'Tracks per-section retrieval strength using localStorage'). The entire app fires exactly ONE analytics event: track('open_app') at components/AnalyticsEvents.jsx:34, and lib/analytics.js only forwards if a provider script happens to be on the page. Anonymous traffic is invisible; the 211 signed-in students are the only observable population.
problems.fix: Add a half-packet before any content work: 6 server-written events (section_open, pretest_shown, pretest_skipped/submitted, step_view{n}, step_complete{n}, section_complete) and check/log upsert errors. Then move P3 (progress truth) ahead of P2. Also define the detection floor: with 1093 starts you can see a step-0 pass move from ~25% to ~40% within two weeks; you cannot see a 3-point move, so only ship big swings first.

problems.problem: Nothing brings a lapsed student back and the plan adds nothing until week 3+. There is no email or push dependency in the project at all, so 'week 3' means 'design, build and warm a sending channel in week 3', which reaches the current cohort's renewal decision after it has already happened. This answers question (3): re-entry has to exist in week 1.
problems.evidence: package.json dependencies are @ai-sdk/google, @supabase/*, ai, framer-motion, next, react*, react-markdown, remark-gfm, stripe — no resend/sendgrid/postmark/nodemailer/web-push. Grep for those names across the repo hits only audit/raw/*.json (the findings themselves). Live pricing is £1 first month then £1.99/month (app/upgrade/page.js:45-59), so the churn decision lands at day ~28-30 after signup — a week-3 build misses every currently-trialling student's first renewal.
problems.fix: Ship 'Re-entry v0' in week 1, deliberately ugly: one transactional provider + a Supabase scheduled function + three plain-text sends — D+2 'you left section X at step N', D+7 'you have K cards due', D+25 'here is what you did this month' before the £1→£1.99 step-up. No design system, no preference centre, no streak. Streak and onboarding can stay in week 3; the win-back cannot.

problems.problem: The plan's pricing premise is stale, and it misses that the freemium BOUNDARY (not the price) is the thing to revisit. This answers question (4).
problems.evidence: The brief says EUR0.99/month, but the live upgrade page sells £1 first month then £1.99/month plus a £12 lifetime (app/upgrade/page.js:5-9, 95-98; components/UpgradePageClient.jsx:70-86), and there is an ungated £6 cancel-save offer (components/CancelOfferModal.jsx:5-16, which documents the real unit economics: 3.33 payments, ~£4.80 net lifetime, Stripe locks customer.currency so EUR customers can only be charged in EUR). That is four prices across two currencies, and the 40/56 cancel figure was measured on a price that no longer exists.
problems.fix: Do not re-cut price now — the £1 trial already suppresses price as a churn cause, and a £12 lifetime cannibalising a £1.99 recurring plan is a separate decision that needs the funnel data first. Do add an explicit week-2 decision packet on the boundary: today the free tier contains the entire teaching surface (Learn Mode, notes, diagrams, practice) and the paid tier is a set of drills the plan barely improves. Either move a paid-tier improvement forward or move a teaching asset behind the wall — but the plan should not go four weeks without asking the question.

problems.problem: Forty people cancelled and zero reasons were recorded, by design. The whole plan is inferring churn cause from a content audit when the cheapest direct evidence is one dropdown.
problems.evidence: components/CancelOfferModal.jsx:5-7 — 'shown to every subscriber who clicks Cancel subscription — no eligibility gating, no reason survey.'
problems.fix: Add a single required reason select to the cancel modal in the same packet as the instrumentation. Five options, one free-text. At 40 cancels/period you get a readable signal inside one month and it costs under an hour.

problems.problem: Mobile localStorage dependence both inflates the 75% and silently resets returning students — the exact failure mode for this cohort. The plan treats the step-0 number as a content problem when part of it is a state-persistence problem.
problems.evidence: showPretest, isComplete (LearnModeTab.jsx:30-37), strength/due-review data (lib/strength.js), and the step fallback `dbStep ?? (localStep ? parseInt(localStep,10) : 0)` (StudyApp.jsx:640-644) are all localStorage. Safari ITP and in-app webviews (Instagram/WhatsApp/Messenger, dominant in PK/LK/HK) clear or partition it, so a returning student is re-served the pre-test wall and reads in the data as a fresh step-0 death.
problems.fix: P3 moves to position 2 and must cover pretest-seen, completion and review schedule server-side, not just furthest_step. Then re-baseline the 75% before judging any content packet.

problems.problem: The due-review retention loop is already built but only visible to students who already came back, and the plan files 'due-review surfacing' under week 3+ as if it were new build.
problems.evidence: components/StudyApp.jsx:324-337 — dueReviewCount is computed from localStorage via countDueReviews() and refreshed on tab change; it is passed only into LearnModeTab (:703), i.e. it renders inside the tab a lapsed student never opens.
problems.fix: Move it server-side as part of P3 and surface the count on Home and in the D+7 email. This is a near-free retention loop that already exists; it should not be sitting in week 3.

problems.problem: P8-P10 order the nine rewrites by audit grade and unit ('Unit 3 Business first'), not by traffic. The two entry sections that lose 87% and 82% are named in the brief as the worst leaks and no packet is scoped to them.
problems.evidence: PLAN_v1.md:38-39 — 'The nine rewrite sections — three packets of three, Unit 3 Business first.' Nothing in the packet list references the two entry sections.
problems.fix: Re-order the rewrite packets by section open volume and put the two entry sections in the first rewrite packet regardless of unit. Those two sections see more traffic than the other seven combined; a C-grade section nobody opens is worth less than a C-grade section everybody opens.

problems.problem: P2 bundles the single highest-leverage change with six cosmetic fixes in one solo packet. If the session runs long, the step-shape change is what gets cut, because the small fixes feel finishable.
problems.evidence: PLAN_v1.md:29-30 — P2 contains step shape, pre-test optional, practice index bug, diagram matching, duplicate recall, 5 unfinishable fill-ins, sticky Next, duplicate subsection title.
problems.fix: Split into P2a (pre-test gate + step shape + sticky Next — the step-0 packet) and P2b (index bug, diagram matching, duplicate recall, fill-ins, duplicate title), and merge P2b into P13 mobile/rendering.

problems.problem: P5's 'shuffled at render' fix will miss the screen that matters most if it is scoped to the quiz bank and the Quiz tab.
problems.evidence: components/learn-mode/PreTest.jsx:7-11 picks 3 questions itself and renders options in bank order with letters A-F; InlineQuiz and QuizTab render separately.
problems.fix: Scope P5's render-time shuffle to all three consumers — PreTest, InlineQuiz, QuizTab — and assert it in validator v2.

problems.problem: An unnamed external human sits on the critical path of every content packet, with no SLA. A week-2 packet cannot ship if sign-off takes a week.
problems.evidence: PLAN_v1.md:59 — 'One IAL teacher signs off rewritten sections and reshaped practice questions before they go live.'
problems.fix: Name the teacher, agree a turnaround, and ship behind a flag so the packet completes even when review is pending. Otherwise the token-conservation plan is gated on a calendar you do not control.

resequencing: Insert a new P0.5 'Measure or don't bother' before all content work: 6 server-written funnel events (section_open, pretest_shown, pretest_submitted/skipped, step_view, step_complete, section_complete), error-checking on the progress upsert, and a required reason select on CancelOfferModal. Reason: the 75% comes from a silently-failing write path and only one analytics event exists in the whole app (AnalyticsEvents.jsx:34), so today no packet can be proven to have worked and the cancel reasons are being inferred from a content audit.

Move P3 (progress truth) from fourth to second, ahead of P2. Reason: resume, pretest-seen and due-reviews are all localStorage on an ITP/webview-heavy mobile cohort, so returning students are re-served the step-0 wall and read as fresh deaths; the baseline is wrong until this lands.

Split P2 and promote P2a 'Step 0 gate' to third: pre-test becomes opt-in or a single predict-question, first card set shortened, one subsection per step, sticky Next. Reason: LearnModeTab.jsx:249 shows step 0 IS the pre-test for any section with quiz data, so the step-shape change alone never reaches the screen that kills 75%. Fold P1's 14 critical error fixes into this session; they do not need their own packet.

Move P5 (quiz hygiene incl. shuffle at render, covering PreTest + InlineQuiz + QuizTab) to fourth. Reason: it is the ONLY packet that improves a paid surface (quiz is a preview/paid tab) and it simultaneously fixes the pre-test screen that step 0 depends on — two numbers per session.

Insert 'Re-entry v0' as fifth, still week 1: one transactional provider, a Supabase scheduled function, three plain sends (D+2 unfinished section, D+7 cards due, D+25 pre-renewal), plus the existing dueReviewCount surfaced server-side on Home. Reason: there is no send channel in package.json at all, and with a £1-first-month price the renewal decision lands at day 28-30, so a week-3 build misses the entire current cohort. Streak, onboarding and freemium re-cut can stay in week 3; win-back cannot.

Keep P4 (validator v2) but position it sixth, immediately before the fan-out packets. Reason: its payoff is entirely in making P6-P11 cheap; landing it before the funnel is open buys nothing this week.

Week 2: P6 and P7 (practice reshaping) as planned, but accept the counterfactual — 215 tariff fixes sit behind a funnel that 75% of students never reach, so their expected churn impact this month is near zero. They stay in week 2 only because tariff mismatch is a trust/refund risk in a small tutoring market, not because they move the number. Do not let them displace re-entry infrastructure.

Week 2-3: re-order P8-P10 (nine rewrites) by section open volume with the two entry sections (87%/82% loss) in the FIRST rewrite packet, not by unit. Reason: the current order is audit-grade-driven; traffic-weighted, those two sections outweigh the other seven.

Add a week-2 decision packet on the freemium boundary (not the price): with Learn Mode, notes, diagrams and practice all free (StudyApp.jsx:25) and the paid tier being drills the plan barely touches, decide what the £1.99 actually buys. Leave the price alone — the £1 trial already suppresses price as a churn cause and there are already four live prices across two currencies.

Week 3 unchanged in content but re-justified: P11 accuracy sweep, P12 Business diagrams, P13 mobile/rendering (now carrying P2b), plus the full step redesign, 338 recalls, 340 spec gaps, onboarding and streak.
whatIsGood: Preserve-first / never-re-audit (P0) is the right first packet — the audit is the expensive asset and it is sitting in a temp dir.
'The validator replaces review' is a genuine token lever and correctly identified as week-1 work: 43 sections checked by script instead of 43 agents.
'Workflows only for real fan-out' is the correct discipline; most plans over-parallelise code packets that have no fan-out.
Deferring the 338 recall exercises until after the step redesign is the right dependency call — regenerating them into the current widgets would be paid-for rework.
Running the validator over all 43 sections after every content packet, not just the touched ones, catches cross-section regressions that per-packet checks miss.
Stable item ids and diffs-not-overwrites (quality gate) is the thing that makes a multi-week split survivable; most split plans skip it and lose edits.

critiques.lens: IAL Economics and Business teacher (15 years, WEC11-14 / WBS11-14), assessing what a student working through a unit actually experiences and what I could defend to a parent paying for it

problems.problem: The headline metric the whole plan is sequenced on is produced by broken instrumentation, and the plan never re-measures. /Users/arongijsel/Claude APP/economics-next/components/StudyApp.jsx writes furthest_step on a 1s debounce whenever activeSection and sectionData.content.length exist — regardless of which tab is open (default activeTab is 'overview', line 267). So a row with furthest_step=0 is created by merely opening a section, including by students who never entered Learn Mode. Worse, learnModeSection is initialised from localStorage only in the useState initialiser (line 304) and is never reset when activeSection changes, while the persist effect (lines 402-409) then stamps the OLD section's step number onto the NEW section's localStorage key. '825 of 1093 starts never passed step 0' is therefore part real abandonment, part instrumentation artefact, and cross-section contamination is corrupting resume points.
problems.evidence: StudyApp.jsx:267 (activeTab default 'overview'), :304-308 (mount-only localStorage read keyed by activeSubjectId_activeSection), :402-409 (persist effect overwrites the new section's key), :577-584 (debounced saveProgress fires on activeSection change, not on Learn Mode use). Plan defers all of this to P3, packet four.
problems.fix: Make instrumentation P0, before P1. Gate the debounced save on activeTab==='content' AND a real Learn Mode render; reset learnModeSection when activeSection changes; key the localStorage read to the current section reactively. Then re-run funnel.mjs to produce a clean baseline and record it in the repo. Add a closing packet that re-measures step-0 pass rate against that baseline — otherwise at the end of four weeks nobody, founder or parent, can say whether any of this worked.

problems.problem: Practice questions with non-IAL command words and point-based mark schemes are the only defect in this audit that makes a student WORSE than not using the product. Everything else wastes time; this actively trains the wrong exam behaviour. A student who rehearses 'Outline two effects (4 marks)' and a point-allocated scheme against a levels-marked 10 or 20 marker will write list-style answers in a WEC/WBS paper and lose a grade band on the evaluation strands. The plan schedules this as P6/P7 — packets seven and eight — and leaves the wrong-shaped questions live in the meantime.
problems.evidence: All 215 practice questions use tariffs/command words that do not exist in IAL papers. Audit of introductory-concepts (192 students): 'practice mark schemes are point-allocated rather than IAL levels-based'. price-determination practiceIssues: "'Outline' is not an IAL command word". meeting-customer-needs: 'a 4-mark Define, a 6-mark Explain two, an Outline command word, point-based guidance for levels-marked 10/20-markers'.
problems.fix: Day-one hotfix, before P0: hide every InlinePractice block whose command word is not on the IAL list for that subject. No authoring required, it is a filter. Show 'Practice question being rewritten to IAL format' instead. Then re-enable per section as each section's content packet lands. Do not leave a wrong-shaped mark scheme in front of a student for six weeks because the rewrite is scheduled.

problems.problem: The untaught-quiz-item problem is not confined to four of the nine rewrite sections — it is in roughly 40 of 43 sections, including both entry sections. That breaks the plan's premise for P5 and for the P6/P7-before-P8/P10 ordering. P5's rule is 'off-topic items moved to the section that teaches them', but for dozens of items NO section teaches them; they are spec gaps, and the 340 spec gaps are deferred to week 3+. So P5 will delete or misfile items that the week-3 packet will then have to re-author.
problems.evidence: Sections with explicitly untaught quiz items include introductory-concepts (Q8 free goods, Q15/Q24 factors of production and rewards), supply (joint supply, producer surplus), consumer-behaviour-demand (consumer surplus), aggregate-demand (paradox of thrift, circular-flow injections), business-objectives-strategy (BCG matrix, 8 items), decision-making-techniques (payback, ARR, 9 items), trade-global-economy (8 items). introductory-concepts's own topFix states the choice explicitly: 'either teach free goods / factors of production in block 2 OR remove Q8, Q15, Q24' — a decision that cannot be made before the spec-gap work is scheduled.
problems.fix: Split P5. Mechanical half (shuffle keys at render, dedupe stems, correct wrong keys, stable ids) runs now as a code packet — it is objective and content-independent. The topical half (which block an item belongs to, keep vs delete vs teach) moves inside each section's own content packet, decided once, alongside that section's spec gaps. Same for practice anchoring.

problems.problem: 'Unit 3 Business first' optimises for the audit's grade distribution rather than for any real student. The nine rewrite sections are the worst-graded, but they are not where students are. Unit 1 is where students are, in September, ahead of a January series.
problems.evidence: introductory-concepts 192 users / 167 stuck at step 0; meeting-customer-needs 123 / 101. Those two are 29% of all 1093 section opens. The D-graded sections sit in the tail: business-objectives-strategy 26, market-structures-contestability 24, and assessing-competitiveness, decision-making-techniques, global-markets-expansion, managing-change, role-state-macroeconomy lower still. Nobody is revising A2 Unit 3 Business in September having not done Unit 1; the 16 premium and 40 cancelled users almost certainly entered through introductory-concepts or meeting-customer-needs, and step 0 of those two is the last thing the churned cohort saw.
problems.fix: Do ONE D-graded section first as a format pilot only — decision-making-techniques, since it has the least worth preserving and 9 untaught quiz items make the rewrite unambiguous. Then strictly traffic order: introductory-concepts, meeting-customer-needs, consumer-behaviour-demand, the-market, planning-raising-finance, types-sizes-businesses, marketing-mix-strategy, supply, price-determination. Also flag revenue-costs-profits (25 users, 1 completion, 5% average progress) and market-structures-contestability (24 users, 1 completion) as effectively dead sections that need the same treatment.

problems.problem: Deferring all 338 recalls to week 3+ means the two sections 315 of 211 students actually touch have, between them, exactly one sound retrieval exercise for the entire remediation period — in a product whose named differentiator is Learn Mode retrieval.
problems.evidence: meeting-customer-needs (123 users, second by traffic) has ZERO recall widgets across 15 subsections — the audit's own words: 'the spaced/immediate retrieval mechanic that defines Learn Mode never fires'. introductory-concepts (192 users, first by traffic) has 10 recalls of which exactly 1 is graded genuine-sequence; the rest are weak-or-arbitrary-sequence, not-orderable, ambiguous-answers, trivial or hint-leaks-answer. types-sizes-businesses (34), revenue-costs-profits (25), business-objectives-strategy (26) also have zero.
problems.fix: Do not do 338 now — do about 30. Six to eight per section for the top six sections by traffic, authored as DATA ({prompt, items, answer, distractors, type}) not as widget markup, inside each section's content packet. The deferral argument is only valid if your recall schema cannot survive a layout change; if that is true, fix the schema in P4 and say so. Note also that the audit's prescribed fix for the bad recalls is a change of TYPE (reorder to sort/match, e.g. 'efficient/inefficient/unattainable point tagging', 'shift vs movement sorting'), so the new widget types are a prerequisite for the entry sections regardless — they belong in P2/P4, not week 3.

problems.problem: The plan is structured as artefact-type sweeps across all units (P5 all 43, P6 all Economics, P7 all Business, P8-P10 nine sections, P11 sweep, P12 sweep), which guarantees that at EVERY point between now and the end, every unit is partially fixed and no unit is coherent. A student does not work across the app; they work down a unit for a mock. The unit of coherence is WEC11 or WBS11, not the app.
problems.evidence: Packet definitions P5-P12 in PLAN_v1.md. Consequence: a student in WBS11 meets a levels-based mark scheme in one section and a point-based one in the next, a recall widget in one and none in the next, a market-map diagram in one and the same topic bare in another.
problems.fix: Restructure into unit-complete packets. One section, end to end: spec gaps, quiz tagging, practice, recalls, diagrams, examples, in one pass, one section per session, traffic order. At the end of week 1 you have one whole unit you can point a class at and one unit you cannot — which is also your only realistic A/B test of whether the content work moves the funnel. To answer the question directly: yes, unsignalled inconsistency is worse than uniform mediocrity, because a student who meets one good mark scheme and one bad one concludes the good one was luck and stops trusting all of them. Bounded, labelled inconsistency ('WEC11 rebuilt, WEC13 in progress') is fine and honest.

problems.problem: The plan's 2-4 week envelope does not contain the work. The explicitly deferred pile — 338 recalls, 340 spec gaps, the 8-stage step redesign, onboarding and reminders — is larger than P0-P13 combined, and its landing window collides with the January series.
problems.evidence: content-work-flat.json: 1170 items — structure 401, specGap 340, topFix 215, quiz 79, accuracy 79, practice 56. P0-P13 is 14 packets at one per session; the deferred set is 678+ items plus a redesign. Today is 11 Sept 2026. Fourteen sessions ends early October; the deferred work lands November-December, i.e. during the January-series revision peak, when changing content under students mid-revision is worse than leaving it.
problems.fix: State an honest freeze date: whatever is not shipped by roughly 1 November is for the June cohort, not January. Then choose what January students get, which forces the traffic-order restructure above. Do not present '2-4 weeks' to the founder as covering the deferred pile.

problems.problem: The human sign-off gate — the only judgement gate in the plan — has no capacity behind it and will be waived. 'One IAL teacher signs off rewritten sections and reshaped practice questions' is nine sections plus 215 practice items plus, later, 338 recalls.
problems.evidence: Single line at PLAN_v1.md:59, no name, no hours, no rate, no position in the packet sequence.
problems.fix: Name the person, book the hours (realistically 25-40 hours for the P6-P10 scope alone), and put the review INSIDE each section packet rather than as a trailing gate. If the answer is 'the founder reviews it', the gate is not independent and should not be written as if it were. Budget it as a line item; at 16 premium x EUR0.99 the product cannot fund it from revenue, so the founder needs to know it is an out-of-pocket cost.

problems.problem: P11 (internationalise UK-domestic examples) as a separate late sweep will redo work that P6/P7/P8-P10 just did, and leaves the credibility problem live in the entry sections for six weeks. For a student in Karachi or Dubai, opening the first section of the course and reading about the NHS, the ONS, HS2 and 'the UK is a mixed economy' is the moment they decide this is a UK product they are borrowing.
problems.evidence: introductory-concepts audit: 'examples are heavily UK-domestic (ONS, NHS x2, HS2, Bank of England, the UK is a mixed economy) for a Hong Kong/Singapore/Pakistan audience'. external-influences: 'CMA/competition law is UK-specific'. P7 authors Business extracts; P11 then internationalises them.
problems.fix: Delete P11 as a standalone sweep. Internationalisation is a rule inside every content packet and a validator check (flag UK-only institutions). Keep a small residual sweep only for sections no content packet touches. Do the entry-section examples as part of the day-one hotfix if they can be swapped as strings.

problems.problem: P7 ('Business practice, every item anchored to an extract') is sized as one packet but is the largest authoring job in the plan and is not comparable to P6. WBS papers are extract-driven; authoring 20 sections' worth of usable stimulus means 20-40 extracts of 150-300 words each with plausible data, internationalised, and each needs its own levels grid.
problems.evidence: P7 as written: '20 sections, every item anchored to an extract', one packet, one workflow. Compare P6: 23 sections reshaped to existing tariffs, no new stimulus required.
problems.fix: Split P7 by unit and fold it into the per-section packets. An extract is section content, not a question attribute, and it has to be written by whoever writes the section.

problems.problem: Mobile (P13) runs last, after every content packet has been authored and reviewed against a layout that is about to change — for a mobile-heavy cohort, on steps that are 5,900px tall.
problems.evidence: P13 is packet fourteen of fourteen. Median 613 words per step plus quiz, practice, explain box, takeaway and two recalls; introductory-concepts audit: 'That is 7-8 interactions on one screen for step 1 of a first-topic section, which is consistent with 167/192 users never leaving step 0.'
problems.fix: Merge P13 into P2. 'A step is readable on a 390px phone' is the acceptance criterion for the step split, not a separate later concern. Every content packet after that is then authored against the real layout.

problems.problem: The validator (P4) risks encoding UK GCE tariffs because only half the units' papers are present as evidence, and the plan's gate says 'practice tariffs from the IAL list for that subject and unit' without saying where that list comes from.
problems.evidence: Scratchpad holds wec11_ms.txt, wec13_ms.txt, wbs11_que.txt, wbs13_que.txt — four of eight units. Nothing for WEC12, WEC14, WBS12, WBS14. db/command_words.json is a generic Define/State/Identify list with no unit or tariff mapping.
problems.fix: Seed the validator's tariff and command-word table from actual WEC11-14 and WBS11-14 papers and mark schemes, all eight units, and store it in the repo as data with the source paper cited per row. Do not let it generalise from four units. This is the single artefact most likely to be quietly wrong in a way that survives every later check, because the validator is the thing you have decided to trust instead of review.

problems.problem: The plan changes step counts (P2, one subsection per step) before it fixes progress persistence (P3), with no migration. Every existing progress row's total_steps becomes wrong and every resume point moves.
problems.evidence: P2 'one subsection per step' precedes P3 'store furthest step against real step count'. LearnModeTab.jsx computes progressPct as ((currentStep+1)/totalSteps)*100 and shows 'You left off at step N of M'; StudyApp.jsx:54 computes dashboard percentage the same way.
problems.fix: Order P3 before or with P2, and ship a migration that rebases furthest_step to the new step count — or accept the reset deliberately and show an in-app note. Do not let a returning student be told 'you left off at step 4 of 11' when step 4 is now a different sentence.

problems.problem: P1, P2 and P3 push content changes before stable item ids exist (P4), so the first three packets are overwrites with no diff — exactly what the plan's own quality gate says must not happen.
problems.evidence: PLAN_v1.md:58 'Pushes become diffs, not overwrites, once items have stable ids' vs P4 landing fourth.
problems.fix: Move stable ids into P0 with the preservation work. They are a data migration, not a validator feature.

problems.problem: Nothing in the plan addresses the free/premium boundary, which is currently doing more reputational harm than EUR15.84/month of revenue is worth.
problems.evidence: introductory-concepts: '20 of 25 MCQs exist only for the pre/post-test random draw and the paywalled Quiz tab'; the extras chain that carries capital vs consumer goods is paywalled; ExplainItBack is premium-gated. So the paying student's exclusive content is a bank containing wrongly keyed and untaught items.
problems.fix: Unpaywall the quiz bank and extras until they pass validator v2, and stop taking new premium signups while any paid surface fails the minimum bar below. Refund on request without argument. Charging for the worst-verified content is the hardest single thing to defend to a parent.

resequencing: HOTFIX, before P0, hours not sessions: disable the pre-test gate globally (LearnModeTab.jsx:249 replaces step 0 entirely with PreTest — this IS the step-0 wall); pull the 6 false examples and 8 wrongly keyed quiz items; hide every practice block whose command word is not on the IAL list. All three are deletions or flags, no authoring, and they remove the negative-value surface immediately.

New P0 = preserve + stable item ids + instrumentation repair. Fix the furthest_step write path in StudyApp.jsx (gate on activeTab==='content' and real Learn Mode render; reset learnModeSection on section change; fix the cross-section localStorage key), then re-run the funnel to produce a clean baseline committed to the repo.

Merge P2 and P13 into one packet: step split to one subsection per step AND the mobile pass (contrast, tap targets, text size, diagram sizing), so every later content packet is authored against the final layout. Also, in this packet, restrict the pre-test draw to items whose tagged subsection exists in the section — a filter, one line, rather than waiting for P5.
P3 progress truth immediately after P2, with a migration rebasing furthest_step to the new step count, or a deliberate reset with an in-app note.

P4 validator next, seeded from all eight units' WEC11-14 / WBS11-14 papers and mark schemes committed as repo data with per-row source citation — not from the four unit papers currently in the scratchpad.

Split P5: mechanical half (render-time key shuffle, dedupe, wrong keys, off-topic detection only) ships as a code packet here; topical re-tagging and keep/delete/teach decisions move into each section's own content packet.

Replace P6, P7, P8-P10, P11 and P12 with one-section-end-to-end packets — spec gaps, quiz tagging, practice with levels grids, 6-8 recalls, diagrams, internationalised examples, all in one pass per section. Sequence: decision-making-techniques as the format pilot, then introductory-concepts (192 users), meeting-customer-needs (123), consumer-behaviour-demand (52), the-market (44), planning-raising-finance (35), types-sizes-businesses (34), marketing-mix-strategy (32), supply (30), then the rest by traffic, D-graded A2 sections last.

Pull roughly 30 recall exercises forward into the entry-section packets, authored as data, and keep the remaining 300-odd deferred. Move the sort/match widget types into P2/P4 since the entry-section fixes require them anyway.
Fold internationalisation into every content packet as a rule plus a validator check; delete P11 as a standalone sweep.

Add a closing packet the plan does not have: re-measure the funnel against the P0 baseline. If step-0 pass rate has not moved, the content work was not the constraint and the next four weeks should go somewhere else.
whatIsGood: Preserve-first, never re-audit, is correct, and the audit artefacts are good enough to work from — per-item recall verdicts with reasons, per-question quiz issues, named spec gaps. Losing that to a temp-dir cleanup would be the single most expensive thing that could happen.

'The validator replaces review' is the best idea in the document and landing it in week 1 is right. It is also the thing most likely to be silently wrong, which is why its seed data matters more than its code.
Making the pre-test optional and remembered is the highest-leverage single change in the plan. It is currently packet three; it should be a same-day flag.
One subsection per step directly attacks the 5,900px step, and the audit's own structural note ties that step weight to 167 of 192 students never leaving step 0. Right diagnosis.

The instinct behind deferring recalls — don't regenerate content into widgets you are about to replace — is the correct dependency reasoning. The conclusion (write zero recalls for a month) is wrong, but the reasoning is not.
Insisting on a human IAL sign-off at all, in a plan otherwise built on automated gates, is the right judgement. It just needs a name and booked hours.
Refusing to use workflows for things that do not fan out (P4 operating rule) is disciplined and will save real money.

critiques.lens: Accountable for not repeating March 2026: would this plan's quality gate catch a repeat? (validator completeness, human sign-off resourcing, regression protection, golden set, content truth vs rule compliance)

problems.problem: The gate has no enforcement point. 'Nothing goes live that validator v2 rejects' is a convention, not a mechanism — content reaches production without ever touching a validator. March had a validator too.
problems.evidence: No /Users/arongijsel/Claude APP/economics-next/.github/workflows, no .husky, and package.json scripts are only dev/build/start. Content ships two ways, neither validated: (a) ~45 one-off scripts/update-*.mjs and upgrade-content-*.mjs doing .update({ data: CONTENT }) with the service-role key via scripts/_db.mjs; (b) PUT /api/admin/sections/[id]/[type]/route.js, which auth-checks the admin role and then upserts request.json() straight into the table with zero schema or semantic checks. The existing check script, scripts/check-learn-content.mjs, prints a green tick for every section regardless of content: it does `const steps = Array.isArray(row.data) ? row.data : []` but row.data is an object ({meta, content, quiz, practice, ...}), so steps is always [] and every section reports '0 steps, 0 concepts ✅'. That is the 2026 equivalent of counting characters, and it is in the repo today.
problems.fix: Put the validator inside the write path, not beside it: one writeSection(sectionId, table, data) in scripts/_db.mjs that validates and throws before upsert, the same validator module imported by the admin PUT route and returning 422 on violation, plus `npm run validate` wired into a GitHub Action and a nightly run against prod (content changes without a commit, so CI-on-push alone is blind). Delete or fix check-learn-content.mjs in P0 so nobody trusts its ticks.

problems.problem: The validator specification is incomplete. It lists nine checks; the mechanically-catchable defect classes in this content need roughly thirty-five, and the largest measured defect (step length, which drives the 75% step-0 drop) has no check at all.
problems.evidence: Gate lists: reorders from real chains, fill-in uniqueness, distractor banks, no letter hints, key position balance, no duplicate stems, quiz tagged to teaching subsection, tariffs from an IAL list, diagram refs resolve. Nothing about step length, schema validity, cross-table integrity, orphaned items, missing fields, cross-section copy-paste, or UK-domestic leakage. Measured from the dump at scratchpad/db/sections (43 files): quiz items have keys [options, question, explanation, correctIndex] and 0 of 769 carry an id; 50 of 215 practice items have NO command field at all (the plan says every item uses wrong command words — a quarter have none); practice marks take exactly four values 4/6/10/20 (83/46/43/43) and commands are Outline 30 / Analyse 4; recall is 131 reorder + 141 fillin, of which 5 fillins already have duplicate answers within one item; 1 quiz item has duplicate option text; only 4 stems duplicate exactly (so a naive duplicate-stem check finds almost nothing — near-duplicate detection is what is needed); 115 blocks pin quiz by array index via quizIndices.
problems.fix: Add these named checks. QUIZ: correctIndex present, integer, in range (the 8 broken items in P1 are this); exactly 4 non-empty options, no all/none-of-the-above; duplicate AND near-duplicate option text (normalised, ≥0.9 similarity); duplicate AND near-duplicate stems across the whole 769-item bank, not per section; key-position balance per section and per subject bank (no position >30% over ≥20 items) AND a unit test proving the render function shuffles — a balanced bank with an unshuffled render is still memorisable; longest-option-is-key heuristic (key >1.4x median option length); key is the only hedged option ('tends to', 'usually'); explanation must not say 'Option B'/'the second option' (breaks after shuffle) and must restate the key's content; stem must not contain the key verbatim (≥6-token shingle overlap); distractor not a negation-only variant of the key; every quizIndices index resolves and every quiz item is referenced by exactly one block (count the orphans); topic pinning computed, not asserted — key terms of the item must match the pinned subsection body or glossary_terms.json, with a stated threshold. PRACTICE: command present (50 currently missing); command ∈ allow-list per subject × unit × paper, the allow-list generated from the real mark schemes already dumped (scratchpad/wec11_ms.txt, wec13_ms.txt, wbs11_que.txt, wbs13_que.txt) and committed as data with provenance, never hand-typed; marks ∈ allow-list for that command and unit (catches 'Define' at 20); marks field must equal the '(n marks)' embedded in the question string (two sources of truth today); guidance must be levels/AO-based for 10 and 20 mark Assess/Evaluate, reject point-scoring '(1 mark)' lists at those tariffs; Business items must carry a resolving extract ref (add the field or the check cannot exist); per-section tariff spread — reject a section whose practice set is one tariff repeated; per-section command concentration >50% flagged. RECALL: reorder items must declare a chainId resolving to a real flow block (body has type:'flow') and correctOrder must be a subsequence of it; parallel-not-sequential proxy — reject when adjacent steps share no lexical carry-over or causal connective, i.e. the items are a list; shuffled must be a permutation, length-matched, not equal to correctOrder, and regenerated at render; 3-5 steps, ≤12 words per step. Fill-ins: answers unique (5 fail now); blank count equals answer count (this is P2's '5 unfinishable fill-ins' and it is mechanical); every answer appears in the subsection body or glossary or the item is unanswerable; ≥2 distractors per blank, none equal to an answer after normalisation; hint leakage as revealed-letters ÷ answer-length with a hard 0.25 ceiling and preferably 0, plus a check that the rendered blank width is fixed rather than answer.length (that leak lives in the renderer, not the data); recall answer must not be the subsection keyIdea verbatim; every subsection must have ≥1 recall so the 24 empty sections fail rather than pass silently. CROSS-CUTTING: per-table JSON Schema/zod with required fields; referential integrity across all eight tables in TABLE_MAP (section_content, section_quiz, section_practice, section_diagrams, section_notes, section_flashcards, section_common_mistakes, section_extras) in both directions; step length budget in words and estimated px with a hard cap, stricter for the two entry sections losing 87% and 82%; duplicate subsection ids; placeholder detection (TODO, [insert, empty strings); cross-section near-duplicate prose via shingle hashing (43 sections in 72 hours leaves that signature); non-IAL leakage (GCSE, AQA, OCR, Ofqual, 'A-level' without 'International', UK-only institutions as defaults, GBP-only examples) for the HK/SG/MY/PK/LK/ME cohort; undated relative time ('currently', 'last year') and examples older than ~3 years; glossary term definitions consistent across sections (hash per term); keep the '<letter' tag-start check from scratchpad/check2.mjs, which silently swallows text; after P4, id stability invariants (unique, never reused, no silent id changes).

problems.problem: 'One IAL teacher signs off' is a line item with no person, no rate, no date, no scope, no accept/reject rule and no blocking behaviour — and at the implied cost it will not happen, so its absence silently becomes the absence of a gate.
problems.evidence: Plan line 59. Scope implied: 9 rewritten sections plus 215 reshaped practice items. At ~20-30 min per section and ~5 min per practice item that is roughly 20-25 hours of qualified time, i.e. four figures against a product with 16 premium users at EUR0.99/month (about EUR16 MRR). Nothing in P0 recruits anyone, yet sign-off gates P8-P10 in week 3. The sign-off also excludes the two largest defect pools entirely: 769 quiz items and 272 recall exercises get no human eyes under this plan.
problems.fix: Resource it in P0 as a named task: source an Edexcel IAL examiner or IAL tutor (Pearson examiner network, HK/SG tutoring marketplaces, the founder's school contacts, or a current user's teacher), agree an hourly rate and a fixed 2-hour scoping session in week 1 so the reviewer's rubric exists before generation starts, and book the review slot for week 3 in advance. Define sign-off as a per-item accept/reject against a written rubric with a recorded reason, not a verbal yes. Write the no-teacher rule explicitly: unsigned sections ship behind a visible 'Draft — under review' flag and are excluded from the paywalled tier, so the gate blocks the claim, not the fix. Fallbacks that are genuinely independent, in priority order: (1) Mark-scheme grounding — every practice item must cite a real question it mirrors (paper code, series, question number) from the papers already dumped in the scratchpad; the item either matches a real question's command+tariff+levels pattern or it does not, which is auditable by the founder in minutes and needs no model judgement. (2) Cold adversarial attempt — a separate model answers each item with no guidance, no key, and no section text, N=3; an MCQ answered correctly >90% of the time cold has non-functional distractors, an MCQ where the cold model consistently picks a distractor probably has a wrong key, a fill-in the cold model cannot produce from the subsection alone is unanswerable. That is a measurement, not the same model grading itself. (3) Real students — 211 signed-in students exist; ship revised items to a slice and flag any MCQ scoring >95% or below the 25% chance floor. (4) Different-model judge given only the spec and mark scheme, blind to the generation prompt, with its agreement rate against the teacher's sample tracked so you know what its verdicts are worth. (5) Founder-executed stratified 10% sample per packet with accept-on-zero: one critical error in the sample fails the packet. Spotting 'this statistic is false' does not require a teacher.

problems.problem: There is no regression protection at all: no version control over content, no baseline, no rollback, no concurrency control. Nothing stops packet 9 from breaking packet 5 and nothing would reveal it if it did.
problems.evidence: The repo's last commit is f3780e3 and predates all content work; 43 sections × 8 tables live only in Supabase, so content changes leave no diff. The only snapshot in existence is the temp-dir dump P0 rescues. The admin PUT route does a blind read-then-update with no updated_at or version check, and the update scripts do .update({data}) unconditionally — last writer wins per table, with no transaction across the eight tables, so a section whose section_content is rewritten by P8-P10 and whose section_quiz was rewritten by P5 can desync without error. 'Every content packet ends with the validator run over all 43 sections' produces a violation count that is compared to nothing.
problems.fix: Four things. (a) Make the repo the source of truth: commit db/sections (and the per-table split) in P0, re-dump and commit at the start and end of every packet, and make every push idempotent from the committed file — then 'did packet 9 break packet 5' is git diff, and rollback is re-pushing the previous file. (b) Store a baseline of violation counts per check per section, committed; a packet fails if any check's count rises anywhere, not only where it was touched. (c) Add a version/updated_at column and compare-and-swap on write, so a 43-way fan-out plus a verification agent doing read-modify-write cannot silently clobber. (d) Add a route-level smoke test: all 43 section pages render step 0 without a client exception at 390px — the funnel failure is a rendering and anatomy failure that no JSON validator can see.

problems.problem: Index pinning is the concrete mechanism by which later packets will break earlier ones, and it is live in the data today.
problems.evidence: 115 blocks in section_content carry quizIndices, pinning by array position into section_quiz, which is a separate table written by a separate PUT; 0 of 769 quiz items have an id. P5 removes duplicates, fixes wrong keys and moves off-topic items between sections — every one of those operations silently repoints every quizIndices in the affected section. The same shape applies to practiceIndices and diagramRef.
problems.fix: Split 'stable item ids + pin-by-id migration' out of P4 into its own packet that runs before any packet that mutates item arrays, and make the validator assert 'zero bare index pins remain' as a blocking check. Note that P1 and P2 both push content before ids exist — P2's practice-index and duplicate-recall edits will have to be redone against ids, so either accept that rework explicitly or move the id migration ahead of P2.

problems.problem: The gate contains no check tied to the headline metric. Nothing in it would fail a 613-word, 5,900px step, and no packet has 'the funnel moved' as its acceptance test.
problems.evidence: 75% of section opens never pass step 0; entry sections lose 87% and 82%. The quality gate (lines 53-59) is entirely about item correctness. P2 is the packet aimed at the drop-off and its result is described as 'verifiable' without saying what is verified. scratchpad/funnel.mjs already computes the funnel.
problems.fix: Add the length budget to the validator as a blocking check (a hard cap per step in words and estimated px, tighter for the two entry sections), and make P2's acceptance criterion an explicit funnel re-measure over the same events after a defined observation window, with a stated target for step-0 pass rate. A content fix that does not move 825 lost starts has not landed.

problems.problem: There is no golden set, so the validator itself is untested — which is exactly how a character-counting validator survived March.
problems.evidence: No test directory, no fixtures, no test script in package.json. Validator v2 (P4) is specified as a deliverable with no way to know whether any given rule fires.
problems.fix: Build the fixture set in P0, before the validator, from material already on disk: ~40 real MCQs with known keys and ~20 real practice questions with real commands, tariffs and level descriptors pulled from scratchpad/wec11_ms.txt, wec13_ms.txt, wbs11_que.txt, wbs13_que.txt (with paper/series/question provenance per item), plus ~20 hand-built known-bad items reconstructed from the March failures: ten items with keys all at B, a near-duplicate stem pair, a fill-in with two identical answers, a fill-in with more blanks than answers, a reorder that is a parallel list, a 20-mark 'Define', an example with a false statistic, an orphaned diagramRef. Two uses: as a test suite for the validator (every known-bad caught by a named check, every real exam item passing) run on every validator change with an asserted exact violation count so a rule broken by a schema change is detected; and as a calibration set for any model judge, measuring its precision and recall before it is trusted on 769 items. Keep the fixtures out of every generation prompt to avoid contamination, and inject two known-bad items into each packet's validation input as a poison pill — if the run passes them, the run is void.

problems.problem: The plan has no method for verifying that content is TRUE, only that it is well-formed, and the accuracy packet (P11) is scheduled with no verification method named.
problems.evidence: Of the March damage, validator-class checks would have caught the 64%-at-B and perhaps half the recall defects, and approximately none of the 79 critical-or-high accuracy errors. P11 fact-checks or replaces 73 high-severity examples as a workflow fan-out, with no source requirement, no acceptance threshold and no sampling plan — the same shape as March, at scale.
problems.fix: Make truth checkable by construction, then check it. (a) Schema: realExample becomes {text, source, sourceUrl, asOf, country, currency}; the validator enforces presence, an asOf within ~3 years, and a minimum share of cohort-region examples per section. Presence is mechanical; truth becomes human-verifiable in seconds because claim and source sit together. (b) Tier claims by falsifiability and route each tier: numeric/dated facts and named-entity claims go through a search-grounded verification pass that must return a source agreeing within tolerance or the item fails; definitional and conceptual claims are checked against econ_spec.txt / bus_spec.txt and glossary_terms.json, not against model memory; pedagogical quality goes to the founder sample, the teacher and the student cohort, because no automated check can reach it. (c) Use contradiction-seeking rather than self-assessment: ask a search-grounded model to find one source that contradicts the claim. 'Find a contradiction' is far more reliable than 'is this true?' asked of the same model's own output. (d) Prefer non-decaying claims: structural examples and dated sourced facts over 'currently' statements, with a validator check for undated relative time. (e) Set an acceptance threshold P11 can fail: hand-check a random 30 examples with sources after the sweep and publish the error rate; above ~5% the packet is not done. March's done-criterion was 'it shipped'.

problems.problem: The gate is binary and will be red from the day it lands, which trains everyone to ignore it.
problems.evidence: 'Nothing goes live that validator v2 rejects' plus deliberate deferral of all 338 recall exercises to week 3+ means the recall checks fail 24 sections for absence and ~197 items for quality on every run from P4 onward, in sections that packets 5-13 must ship.
problems.fix: Tier severities: BLOCK (ships nothing), DEBT (allowed, but each accepted violation is recorded with a section, a reason, an owner and an expiry date, and the per-check debt count must only ever go down), INFO. Commit the debt ledger alongside the baseline. A gate that is permanently red is not a gate.

problems.problem: No rollback procedure for content.
problems.evidence: section_content and its seven sibling tables hold a single JSON blob per section with no version history; a bad push from any packet is unrecoverable except by regenerating.
problems.fix: Either add a versions table written on every push, or make git the version history: push only from a committed dump file, never from an inline CONTENT literal in a one-off script, so reverting is a file checkout plus a re-push.

problems.problem: P1 pushes content to production before the validator that is supposed to prove it exists.
problems.evidence: P1 (6 false examples, 8 broken quiz items) and P2 (container fixes, fill-ins, duplicate recall) both precede P4 (validator v2), despite the operating model stating the validator lands in week 1 because it replaces review.
problems.fix: Move validator v2 to packet 1. The P1 items are precisely the class the validator must prove it catches; fixing them by hand first and validating later gets the evidence backwards.

problems.problem: Deferring the recall rewrite until after the step redesign is defensible, but the plan does not say what happens to the 24 sections with zero recall in the meantime, and the sign-off scope excludes recalls and quizzes permanently.
problems.evidence: Lines 47-49 defer 338 recall exercises; line 59 scopes human sign-off to rewritten sections and reshaped practice only. 272 existing recalls of which only 75 are sound remain live for the whole 2-4 weeks.
problems.fix: Decide explicitly whether the 197 unsound recalls stay visible to students during the remediation or are hidden behind a flag until replaced. Add a sampling rule for quizzes and recalls: even without a teacher, the founder reviews a stratified 10-item sample per packet against the cold-attempt results.

problems.problem: The 43-way workflow fan-outs have no per-agent output contract beyond the validator, so an agent that produces well-formed nonsense passes.
problems.evidence: P5, P6, P7, P8-P10 and P11 are all fan-outs; the only named acceptance is the validator run, which by construction checks form.
problems.fix: Give each fan-out agent a required output envelope: the item, its citation (paper/series/question for practice, source/asOf for examples), the cold-attempt result for the items it authored, and a self-declared list of which validator checks it expects to pass. Then the orchestrating session diffs declared-vs-actual and sends back only the mismatches, which is also the cheapest possible verification pass.

resequencing: Move validator v2 (P4) to packet 1, before P1 and P2 push any content. The P1 fixes are the exact class the validator must prove it catches.
Build the golden-set fixtures in P0, before the validator is written, from the already-dumped past papers and mark schemes — the validator should be written against tests, not tested afterwards.

Split 'stable item ids + pin-by-id migration' out of P4 into its own packet immediately after the validator and before P2, because P2's practice-index and duplicate-recall edits are index-pinned and will otherwise be redone.

Add to P0: commit the content dump to git, add npm run validate plus a GitHub Action and a nightly prod run, delete or fix scripts/check-learn-content.mjs (it currently passes every section), and store the first validator baseline and debt ledger.
Start IAL teacher recruitment in P0 as a named task with a rate and a booked date — sign-off gates P8-P10 three weeks out and cannot be arranged retroactively.
Give P2 a measurable acceptance test: re-run funnel.mjs after a defined observation window against a stated step-0 pass-rate target, rather than 'a verifiable result'.
Run P5 only after both the id migration AND a unit test proving render-time shuffle — rebalanced keys in an unshuffled renderer get re-memorised.

Design P11's verification method (source fields on realExample, search-grounded contradiction pass, 30-item hand-checked sample with a stated error-rate threshold) inside the validator packet; as currently sequenced P11 is a 73-item re-run of March with no acceptance criterion.
whatIsGood: Preserve-first: moving every per-item finding into the repo before the temp dir is cleaned is the right first move, and 'no session ever re-derives a finding' is the correct token discipline.
Validator before the fan-outs: encoding rules in code so 43 sections cost a script run rather than 43 agents is the right economics, and the plan recognises it explicitly.
Restricting workflows to genuine fan-out (215 practice items yes, a sorting bug no) is a correct and unusually disciplined call.
Running the validator over all 43 sections after every content packet, not just the touched ones, is the right instinct — it only needs a committed baseline to compare against.
Deferring the 338 recall exercises until after the step redesign so they are not regenerated into the same broken widgets is a genuinely good sequencing judgement.
Keeping the deferred work as an explicit 'not dropped' list with the step anatomy, 340 spec gaps and onboarding named is better than a silent backlog.
'Pushes become diffs, not overwrites, once items have stable ids' correctly identifies stable ids as the precondition for everything else.
